description: Implement the Unix lifecycle backend for Claude batch, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, and Pi. Launch a trusted supervisor in a dedicated process group with a launch gate and parent-liveness control pipe. Preserve PGID and process-birth identity immediately after start. Parent-pipe EOF triggers staged group cleanup after embedding-process death. Normal completion, failure, cancellation, and timeout use the same boundary cleanup path under a context independent of the request context. Bare Pdeathsig is secondary protection only because it does not contain grandchildren. PTY, auxiliary probes, Windows, and service terminal supersession are out of scope.
notes: Implemented shared durable Unix batch lifecycle supervision for Claude (forced subprocess), Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, and Pi. description:
PROBLEM
The parent bead `fizeau-cd9af16b` proposes moving every root-level `package fizeau` file into `internal/service/` and requires zero `.go` files at the module root. Repository evidence conflicts with that plan:
- ADR-008 says the root `package fizeau` is the public facade at `github.com/easel/fizeau` and that the module import path must stay stable.
- The generated embedding docs document the root package as the importable library surface.
- agentcli/, cmd/bench/, cmd/fiz/, and root black-box tests import `github.com/easel/fizeau` directly.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
`docs/helix/02-design/adr/ADR-008-service-package-and-transcript-boundaries.md:43-64` explicitly keeps the root package as the compatibility boundary and moves only concrete implementation code behind `internal/`. `service.go:18-20` defines the root `FizeauService` public interface. `website/content/docs/embedding/_index.md:949-974` documents `github.com/easel/fizeau` as the root facade and lists importable public packages. Therefore parent AC #1 (zero root `.go` files) is not executable without either violating ADR-008 or first designing a replacement public facade.

PROPOSED FIX
Write a cold-readable design/inventory doc under `docs/helix/02-design/` that converts the oversized parent into an ordered extraction plan. The doc must inventory root-level `.go` files, bucket each as public facade, public compatibility alias/shim, or implementation-owned file, list in-repo consumers of `github.com/easel/fizeau`, and name follow-on extraction slices with target internal package owners.

NON-SCOPE
Do not move production Go files in this bead. Do not rewrite imports. Do not update CHANGELOG.md or generated website links beyond whatever is required to land the governing inventory doc itself. Do not remove the root public package.

PARENT AND DEPS
Parent: `fizeau-cd9af16b`. No deps; this bead is the design/inventory prerequisite that makes the parent sequence executable.
title: repo-structure: reconcile root-package move with ADR-008 and inventory facade vs implementation files

description:
PROBLEM
  internal/modelcatalog/manifest.go carries the legacy v4 schema with overlapping concepts: profiles AND targets AND aliases AND surface_policy AND ModelEntry.Tier back-pointers AND compatibility_target redirection. The v0.11 surface redesign collapses this to a single first-class concept (policy) and drops everything else.

ROOT CAUSE
  Manifest accumulated migration debt from prior renames. compatibility_target/target duality is half-done rename cruft (validator at manifest.go:460 says they must match when both set). surface_policy was an attempt to centralize per-(target × harness) defaults that ages poorly once reasoning_default moves to per-model. ModelEntry.Tier is a back-pointer to a target that no longer exists in v0.11.

DESIGN INTENT (v0.11)
  - Top-level keys: models, policies, providers (catalog-side type+include_by_default declarations), sampling_profiles (UNCHANGED, ADR-007).
  - REMOVED: targets:, aliases:, compatibility_target on policies, surface_policy blocks, ModelEntry.Tier field.
  - Each policy: { min_power: int, max_power: int, allow_local: bool, require: []string }.
  - Hard cut on schema version (v4 → v5). External manifests pinned to v4 fail at load with helpful error pointing at ADR-009 (Phase 8).
  - No aliases. The four canonical policy names (default, cheap, smart, air-gapped) are the only valid values. code-economy/code-smart/standard/local/offline/fast/code-fast/code-high/code-medium are removed with no replacement.
  - Validator requires catalog to define a "default" policy (fallback for empty req.Policy).
  - New BillingForProviderSystem and BillingForHarness functions in internal/modelcatalog/billing.go: hardcoded mapping by provider/harness type (lmstudio/llama-server/omlx/vllm/rapid-mlx/ollama/lucebox → fixed; openai/openrouter/anthropic/google → per_token; claude/codex/gemini harnesses → subscription; native fiz harness derives from underlying provider).

CURRENT STATE WITH FILE:LINE
  - internal/modelcatalog/manifest.go:36-76 ModelEntry (with Tier field at line 40)
  - internal/modelcatalog/manifest.go:107-118 manifest struct (Targets, Profiles fields)
  - internal/modelcatalog/manifest.go:120-126 profileEntry
  - internal/modelcatalog/manifest.go:128-218 surfaceValue/targetEntry/surfacePolicyEntry types (~91 lines to delete)
  - internal/modelcatalog/manifest.go:245-487 loadManifest + validateManifest
  - internal/modelcatalog/manifest.go:489-545 upgradeManifest (delete entirely)
  - internal/modelcatalog/manifest.go:577 profileCompatibilityTarget
  - internal/modelcatalog/catalog.go:36,53-69 Catalog struct, Profile/ResolvedTarget types
  - internal/modelcatalog/catalog.go:122-182 Profiles/Profile/Aliases methods

PROPOSED FIX
  1. Drop ModelEntry.Tier field. Add ModelEntry.ReasoningDefault (reasoning.Reasoning type) for per-model intrinsic reasoning posture.
  2. manifest struct: drop Targets, drop Profiles. Add Policies map[string]policyEntry, Providers map[string]providerEntry. No top-level aliases field.
  3. policyEntry: { MinPower int, MaxPower int, AllowLocal bool, Require []string }. providerEntry: { Type string, IncludeByDefault bool, Billing string (optional, required if Type unknown) }.
  4. Delete surfaceValue, targetEntry, surfacePolicyEntry types (~91 lines).
  5. Rewrite validateManifest: max_schema_version = 5; every policy has min<=max valid power range; every provider has type; "default" policy must exist; require[] entries must be in known invariant set ({"no_remote"}); user-config providers with Type not in known catalog set must declare Billing explicitly.
  6. Delete upgradeManifest; v4→v5 is a hard cut. Loader emits "manifest schema v5 required (got v%d); see ADR-009 for v0.11 schema redesign" on version mismatch.
  7. Catalog struct: rename profileEntries → policyEntries. Replace Profile struct with Policy{Name string, MinPower, MaxPower int, AllowLocal bool, Require []string}. Drop ResolvedTarget, SurfacePolicy, MissingSurfaceError, DeprecatedTargetError, UnknownTargetError, Surface enum, ResolveOptions, Resolve, Current, AllConcreteModels, CandidatesFor, AllModelsInTier, TierModel, concreteModelsForSurface, primaryConcreteModel, targetCandidateIDs, deprecatedRoutingGuidance.
  8. Catalog: add Policy(name) (Policy, bool), Policies() []Policy. Drop Aliases() entirely (no aliases concept).
  9. New file internal/modelcatalog/billing.go: BillingModel enum (fixed/per_token/subscription) + BillingForProviderSystem(string) BillingModel + BillingForHarness(string) BillingModel.
  10. Inline-YAML test fixtures in internal/modelcatalog/manifest_test.go and catalog_test.go: rewrite from legacy v4 schema to v5 in lockstep with the production code change.

NON-SCOPE

  - Public service surface — Phase 4.

description:
PROBLEM: ADR-013 §3 (decision item 6, orphan reaper) requires that PTY child processes left alive be reaped on harness shutdown within a bounded timeout, escalating SIGTERM to SIGKILL, so a terminating fiz process does not leak orphaned `claude` PTY children.

ROOT CAUSE:
- internal/harnesses/claude-tui/harness.go:36-149 — the Harness exposes no Shutdown method (only Info/HealthCheck/Execute/Quota/Account/ModelDiscovery), so pooled PTY children are never terminated and nothing enumerates live PTY children at teardown.
- internal/pty/session/types.go:276,293,309 — Session.Close/Kill/Wait exist but are not driven from any harness-level shutdown path; the process-group kill at internal/pty/session/session_unix.go:122-134 is invoked only on context cancel, not on harness teardown.

PROPOSED FIX:
1. Add Harness.Shutdown(ctx) that enumerates the pool's live PTY sessions and reaps each within a bounded timeout: send SIGTERM (Session.Close), then escalate to SIGKILL (Session.Kill) if Session.Wait does not return before the deadline.
2. The reaper inspects live session state only — no persistent or cross-invocation state (ADR-013 §3 item 6).

NON-SCOPE:
- The session pool data structure, reuse, and `/clear`-between-turns logic (sibling child in this decomposition).
- The startup cross-invocation reaper analogous to service_stale_harness_reaper*.go — this bead is the in-process shutdown reaper only.
- The PTY turn driver and intermediate ProgressEvent emission (sibling child A).
- AccountHarness and QuotaHarness implementations (sibling child C).

- Cassette-driven static fallback for production code (forbidden by fizeau-89eca738).
- Service-side changes beyond what child #1 already wired.
- Redesigning the hook-conflict arbitration layer.

Depends on the sibling session-pool child of this decomposition, child #1, and sibling child A. Governing artifacts: ADR-013 §3 (decision item 6), CONTRACT-004, internal/pty/ library.

description:
PROBLEM
Even when the openrouter API key is valid, an account with exhausted credit will fail every dispatch with an insufficient-credit response. Without a proactive credit probe, each request burns a retry to rediscover an account-level condition that does not change between requests.

ROOT CAUSE
There is no openrouter quota/balance probe in the route-picker's freshness-cache layer. `service_routing.go` already exposes `quota_freshness_at` on candidate rows and consults a cached aliveness/quota state so the picker performs no per-call network I/O — openrouter is simply not wired into that cache. Exact integration point to be confirmed during implementation by locating the existing `quota_freshness_at` write path.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Add a periodic openrouter credit probe that calls `GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/credits` (confirm exact path against current openrouter docs at implementation time) using the configured API key.
2. Cache the result in the same freshness-cache module as existing aliveness/quota state, keyed by openrouter provider id. TTL configurable; default in the 5–15 minute range (implementer picks within that band and documents the choice).
3. Configurable balance threshold for `credit_exhausted` (default $0.50). Threshold lives in openrouter provider config; documented alongside other provider knobs.
4. If cached balance is below threshold → candidate `eligible: false`, `filter_reason: "credit_exhausted"`, evidence body includes the observed balance and the probe timestamp.
5. If cached balance is at/above threshold → candidate passes this gate (credential gate handled by [[openrouter-credential-presence-gate]]; failure modes handled by [[openrouter-probe-failure-modes-and-surfacing]]).
6. Route picker reads cached state only — no per-Execute network round-trip to openrouter.ai/credits.

NON-SCOPE
- Credential presence/format checks (covered by [[openrouter-credential-presence-gate]]).
- 401 / transport-failure handling and the credential_invalid / provider_unreachable filter_reasons (covered by [[openrouter-probe-failure-modes-and-surfacing]]).
- Per-model credit-cost forecasting (parent non-scope, preserved).
- Multi-account credential rotation (parent non-scope, preserved).
- DDx-side changes per CONTRACT-003 (parent non-scope, preserved).

CROSS-REF
Sibling beads: [[openrouter-credential-presence-gate]], [[openrouter-probe-failure-modes-and-surfacing]]. Cross-ref fizeau-80d4bf41.
title: openrouter: credit balance probe with TTL cache and configurable threshold

The parent scope requires replacing cmd/bench/matrix.go:1 with scripts/benchmark/benchmark and removing the host Python dependency introduced by cmd/bench/matrix.go:1105. description:
PROBLEM
Fizeau's auto-route includes openrouter as an eligible candidate even when no API key is configured AND/OR the account has zero credit balance. Dispatches that pick openrouter then fail at HTTP-call time with 401 (no auth header) or insufficient-credit errors. Beads burn retry cycles, sticky leases get assigned to a dead provider, and operators must debug a transport error to discover that the actual problem is a missing credential or empty wallet.

This is the same pattern Fizeau already handles correctly for local LMStudio/MLX endpoints: when a local endpoint fails its aliveness probe, it surfaces as `filter_reason: "endpoint_unreachable"` in routing_decision and is excluded from scoring. Openrouter needs an analogous health gate.

EVIDENCE FROM DOWNSTREAM (DDx, commit 09881f3a5)
While debugging fizeau-80d4bf41 (auto-route candidate enumeration), I observed:
1. With `--model sonnet-4.6` pinned, Fizeau routed to `fiz/openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6` with score 196.0 (auto-route's first choice once the model name was known to it).
2. The dispatch then immediately failed: `agent: provider error: openai: POST "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions": 401 Unauthorized {"message":"Missing Authentication header","code":401}`.
3. No upstream filter on the openrouter candidate. It appeared in the candidate list as `eligible: true`, was selected, and the credential failure surfaced only at HTTP call time inside the harness.

Symmetric symptom is expected when credentials exist but credit is exhausted — openrouter returns a 402/insufficient-credit response. Without proactive credit checks, every dispatch through openrouter will burn a retry to discover this.

PROPOSED FIX
Add an openrouter provider-health hook analogous to the LMStudio aliveness probe. The hook should:

1. **Credential check** (cheap, run on every routing pass or cache for a short TTL like 60s):
   - If the openrouter API key environment variable / config is empty or unset → mark openrouter `eligible: false` with `filter_reason: "credential_missing"`. Do not even hit the network.
   - If the configured key is malformed (wrong prefix, wrong length) → same.

2. **Credit check** (more expensive, run periodically — recommend 5-15 minute TTL with stale-allowed-during-grace):
   - Call openrouter's `GET /api/v1/credits` (or whatever the current endpoint is) to fetch remaining credit balance.
   - If balance is below a configurable threshold (default: $0.50) → mark openrouter `eligible: false` with `filter_reason: "credit_exhausted"`, include current balance in the decision evidence.
   - If the credit-check call itself fails with 401 → mark `credential_invalid` (different from missing).
   - If the credit-check call fails with transport error → mark `provider_unreachable` (transient; fail-open with stale-signal-penalty bump rather than hard-excluding, to avoid flapping).

3. **Surface in routing_decision**: candidate row appears with `eligible: false`, `filter_reason` set to one of the values above, and `health_freshness_at` / `quota_freshness_at` populated from the cached probe. This mirrors how `bragi-club-3090` already appears with `endpoint_unreachable` and how `claude-haiku-4.5` appears with `power_missing`.

4. **Cache placement**: probe state should live in the same place as the existing harness aliveness/quota state so the route picker reads it without doing per-call network I/O. `service_routing.go` already has `health_freshness_at` and `quota_freshness_at` fields plumbed through — wire openrouter into that.

NON-SCOPE
- Multi-account credential rotation / failover within openrouter.
- Per-model credit-cost forecasting.
- The DDx-side change is none — this is purely Fizeau-side. DDx passes `policy=default` through unchanged per CONTRACT-003.

CROSS-REF

description:
PROBLEM
Background model discovery refresh can inherit a caller context that has already been cancelled. In stale-while-revalidate mode this means `AssembleWithOptions(... RefreshBackground)` returns stale rows but the refresh goroutine may never reach provider discovery, so stale caches remain stale. Runtime signal warmup also needs to normalize OpenAI-compatible base URLs that already include `/v1` so probes hit `/v1/models` exactly once.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `internal/modelregistry/discovery.go:134-143` and `internal/modelsnapshot/discovery.go:133-142` build provider discovery requests from the caller context when one is present, even for `RefreshBackground` refreshers spawned by the cache.
- `internal/modelregistry/background_refresh_contract_test.go` lacked coverage for a cancelled caller context with stale cached rows.
- `internal/runtimesignals/collect.go:241-247` constructs the local runtime probe URL by appending `/v1/models` directly to `BaseURL`, producing `/v1/v1/models` when the configured base URL already ends in `/v1`.

PROPOSED FIX
For background refresh mode, use the cache refresh context rather than the caller context; for foreground refresh modes, preserve caller cancellation while bounding it by the cache refresh deadline. Mirror the helper in both modelregistry and modelsnapshot until those packages are deduplicated. Normalize local runtime signal base URLs before appending `/v1/models`. Add/keep focused tests for stale-while-revalidate with a cancelled caller and for `/v1` base URL normalization.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx pre-claim readiness needs a "smart/frontier" route, but Fizeau's public routing surface currently exposes overlapping concepts (`profile`, `model_ref`, `model`, `min_power`, `max_power`, and `harness`) with unclear semantics. DDx temporarily switched readiness to `model_ref=smart` in v0.6.2-alpha40 because the installed Fizeau route-status path reported no smart route even though GPT-5.5 was available. That workaround is not an acceptable long-term contract; human input is needed on the Fizeau-side routing API.

USER FEEDBACK
The operator explicitly rejected the current workaround: "model_ref is bullshit". Treat this bead as a design/contract decision gate, not a request to deepen DDx's workaround.

OBSERVED EVIDENCE ON 2026-05-08
- Installed binary: `/home/erik/go/bin/fiz` reports `fiz v0.10.13`.
- Installed binary command:
  `fiz route-status --profile smart --json --work-dir /Users/erik/Projects/ddx`
  returned `candidates: []` and error `no live provider supports prompt of 0 tokens with tools=false at tier >= smart`.
- The same installed catalog advertises smart entries: `fiz catalog show` reports `agent.openai: gpt-5.5` and `agent.anthropic: opus-4.7` under `smart`.
- DDx proved GPT-5.5 was reachable through the workaround path: after installing DDx v0.6.2-alpha40, `ddx run --model-ref smart --harness codex --text 'Reply exactly: alpha40-smart-ok' --timeout 45s` succeeded and session `as-199166d6` recorded `harness=codex`, `model=gpt-5.5`.
- Current Fizeau checkout differs from the installed binary: `./fiz --version` reports `v0.10.12-0.20260506230320-1819c0a582c2+dirty`; `./fiz route-status --profile smart --json --work-dir /Users/erik/Projects/ddx` now returns smart candidates including `claude/opus-4.7` and `agent/openrouter openai/gpt-5.5`.
- In the same checkout, `./fiz route-status --model-ref smart --harness codex --json --work-dir /Users/erik/Projects/ddx` returns `candidates: []` and the same `no live provider ... tier >= smart` error because the codex candidate is currently unhealthy/quota-limited. This shows the surface is also sensitive to quota/health state in a way that produces misleading operator language.

CODE ANCHORS
- `service.go:368-378` defines `RouteRequest` with `Profile`, `Model`, `Provider`, `Harness`, `ModelRef`, `MinPower`, and `MaxPower` side by side.
- `service.go:676-688` defines `ServiceExecuteRequest` with both `ModelRef` and `Profile` exposed publicly.
- `service_routing.go:46-82` threads profile, model-ref, provider preference, and power bounds into internal routing.
- `service_routing.go:1091-1115` maps profile to provider preference.
- `service_routing.go:1117-1150` derives profile power policy but explicitly does not apply it when `Model` or `ModelRef` is set.
- `service_execute.go:296-305` treats `smart`/`code-smart`/`code-high` as subscription-only explicit profile constraints when a harness is pinned.
- `agentcli/routing_smart.go:823-825` exposes both `--profile` and `--model-ref` on `route-status`, making users choose between two smart-ish abstractions.

IMPACT
- Downstream callers can report "no smart model available" while GPT-5.5 is actually reachable through a different Fizeau field.
- DDx readiness can park, skip, or fail-open beads for the wrong reason.
- Operators are forced to know that `model_ref=smart` may work when `profile=smart` does not, which is not a coherent public API.
- Quota/health rejection is currently collapsed into a generic "no live provider" message that hides the existence of smart candidates and the reason they were rejected.

HUMAN DECISION NEEDED
Decide the canonical Fizeau contract for "smart/frontier route": should callers express it as `profile=smart`, numeric power (`min_power` / `max_power`), a catalog alias, or a new intent field? Decide whether `ModelRef` should remain public, become internal, be renamed, or be deprecated. Decide how explicit harness pins interact with smart intent and how route-status/Execute should explain quota/health rejection.

PROPOSED WORK AFTER DECISION
- Amend the Fizeau contract/ADR/docs with the chosen semantics.
- Align `RouteRequest`, `ServiceExecuteRequest`, `route-status`, `Execute`, and CLI help with that contract.
- Add tests for the chosen behavior, especially smart intent with and without explicit `--harness codex`.
- File or update downstream DDx cleanup work to remove the `model_ref=smart` workaround once Fizeau exposes the final surface.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement the routing change in this bead. Do not add another DDx workaround here. This bead is the human decision record that unlocks implementation beads.

notes:
DECISION RECORDED 2026-05-08

Canonical Fizeau routing-surface semantics for v0.11 (decided via design conversation):

PROFILE → POLICY (rename)
  "Policy" is the single canonical word. No aliases (code-economy/code-smart/standard/local/offline/fast/code-fast/code-high/code-medium are dropped with no replacement). Four canonical policies:
    default:    {min_power: 7, max_power: 8, allow_local: true}
    cheap:      {min_power: 5, max_power: 5, allow_local: true}
    smart:      {min_power: 9, max_power: 10, allow_local: false}
    air-gapped: {min_power: 5, max_power: 5, allow_local: true, require: [no_remote]}

MODELREF → REMOVED ENTIRELY
  Hard cut at v0.11.0. No compat period, no deprecated alias. Operators using --model-ref get a cobra "unknown flag" error. ServiceExecuteRequest.ModelRef field is deleted (not deprecated). Catalog ref expansion previously done via ModelRef no longer happens — callers pass concrete Model when pinning, otherwise rely on Policy.

MIN_POWER / MAX_POWER → SOFT SCORING SIGNALS
  Fields preserved but no longer enforced as filters. Scorer applies asymmetric penalties: undershoot 5x worse than overshoot. A power-7 candidate beats a power-11 candidate when both healthy and policy is min:8/max:10. Smart's allow_local: false is what produces fail-closed behavior when subscription is dry, NOT a hard power floor.

HARNESS PINS
  Pin overrides provider.include_by_default (operator can reach excluded providers via pin). Pin does NOT override policy.require[] (--policy air-gapped --provider openrouter fails with ErrPolicyRequirementUnsatisfied). Pin-pin conflicts (harness×model, harness×provider, provider×model) fail with ErrUnsatisfiablePin.

ERROR LANGUAGE FOR THE FOUR ROUTE-STATUS SCENARIOS

  --policy smart (subscription healthy):
    Returns smart candidates from claude/codex/gemini subscription harnesses.

  --policy smart (subscription dry):
    Returns ErrNoLiveProvider with RejectedCandidates populated. Error message: "policy 'smart' has N candidate(s) matching power 9-10 but all rejected: Q quota-exhausted, U unhealthy".

  --policy smart --harness codex (codex healthy):
    Pin to codex; returns the gpt-5.5 candidate.

  --policy smart --harness codex (codex unhealthy/quota-exhausted):
    Returns ErrNoLiveProvider with RejectedCandidates=[{Harness: codex, Reason: quota_exhausted}]. Error message names the specific harness and reason.

  --model-ref smart --harness codex (transition):
    Cobra "unknown flag: --model-ref" error. No transition period.

  Execute({Policy:"smart", Harness:"codex"}):
    Same resolution as --policy smart --harness codex above. Field is Policy not Profile (Go compile error if caller uses Profile).

IMPLEMENTATION BEADS (FILED)

  Phase 1: fizeau-b633cbb3 — internal/routing rename + soft min/max + ModelRef removal + ErrNoLiveProvider quota/health distinction (this addresses the operator-visible error language ask in AC4 of this bead)
  Phase 2: fizeau-040f1f83 — manifest schema redesign + billing.go
  Phase 3: fizeau-0aaa94e5 — catalog/models.yaml v5 rewrite
  Phase 4: fizeau-c6c8bc9e — public service surface
  Phase 5: fizeau-2d0bd0a4 — provider config (include_by_default + Billing)
  Phase 6: fizeau-399ecb48 — CLI surface (fiz policies + fiz harnesses subcommands; --model-ref/--profile flags removed)
  Phase 7: fizeau-9eb62a07 — internal/core ModelRef removal + telemetry/session-log schema break
  Phase 8: fizeau-264e70c4 — ADR-009 + CONTRACT-003 + FEAT-003/004/005/006 rewrites (this is where the canonical semantics get committed to a Fizeau design document, satisfying AC1)
  Phase 9: fizeau-32e533bb — DDx coordination (drop --model-ref, rename Profile→Policy in DDx call sites; satisfies AC5's downstream cleanup)

AC SATISFACTION TABLE

  AC1 (semantics in design doc) → Bead 8 produces ADR-009.
  AC2 (covers Profile/ModelRef/Model/MinPower/MaxPower/Harness) → all named above; ADR-009 documents each.
  AC3 (ModelRef fate + compat period) → removed entirely, no compat. Beads 1/4/5/6/7/9 implement; Bead 8 documents.
  AC4 (route-status + Execute behavior) → Beads 1, 4, 6; ErrNoLiveProvider enhancement in Bead 1 specifically addresses the "operator-visible error language" concern.
  AC5 (follow-up implementation beads) → the nine beads above.
  AC6 (go test not required) → N/A; decision-only.

This bead can be closed by the human reviewer once the decision above is acceptable. Implementation tracks via the nine listed beads.

description:
First and largest piece of the bench runner rewrite. Replaces cmd/bench/matrix.go with
a bash runner; ports the matrix-side Python harness_adapters/ to shell harness-adapters/;
wraps Harbor invocation in a Docker container so the host stops needing Python.

CONTEXT: today's runner is `fiz-bench matrix` (Go, cmd/bench/matrix.go ~2232 LOC). It
puts repo root on host PYTHONPATH (cmd/bench/matrix.go:1105) so Harbor can import
scripts.benchmark.harbor_adapters.*. That makes host Python required. We're moving
Harbor and its plugins into a fizeau-harbor-runner Docker image so the host only needs
bash + Node + Docker. The new runner is at scripts/benchmark/benchmark (no extension).

SCOPE — runner (scripts/benchmark/benchmark, new bash script):
  - Arg parsing + dispatch: ./benchmark <subcommand> ... with subcommands
      profiles | bench-sets | task-executors | harness-adapters | validate |
      preflight | (no subcommand = run mode)
  - Run mode flags: --profile P[,P2,...] --bench-set B[,B2,...] [--plan]
      [--force-rerun] [--retry-invalid] [--reps N] [--jobs N] [--max-cost-usd X]
      [--out DIR]
  - Read profile/bench-set/concurrency-group YAML with `yq -o=json`.
  - Matrix expansion: profile × task × rep -> ordered cell list. Resolve `tasks_from:`
    references (path relative to bench-set file) AND inline `tasks:` lists. PR C will
    finalize the schema; for PR A's smoke tests, default `task_executor` to `harbor`
    when `framework == terminal-bench`.
  - Resume default: if cell_dir/report.json exists with terminal final_status -> skip.
    --force-rerun ignores. --retry-invalid reruns cells with non-empty invalid_class OR
    orphan cell-state.json.
  - Per-cell loop: write cell-state.json sentinel; invoke
    harness-adapters/<name> command < profile.json -> command-spec.json; compose
    task-spec; invoke task-executors/<name> < task-spec.json (writes
    cell_dir/result.json); compose report.json; delete cell-state.json.
  - Concurrency: flock per concurrency-group at
    \${FIZEAU_BENCH_STATE_DIR:-\${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-\$HOME/.cache}/fizeau-benchmark}/locks/<group>.lock;
    setsid for each cell process group; background-job pool capped by --jobs.
  - Signal handling: trap SIGINT/SIGTERM. Stop accepting new cells. SIGTERM each
    in-flight cell's process group and `docker stop` each in-flight harbor-runner
    container. Wait 30s, then SIGKILL. Write final_status=interrupted to in-flight
    cells (process_outcome=killed, no metrics). Exit non-zero.
  - Concurrent-cells state file at
    \${FIZEAU_BENCH_STATE_DIR}/<hostname>/in-flight.json. Runner appends its cell at
    start under flock, reads current count, writes into cell, removes at close.
    Prune stale entries (PID dead) at next read.
  - Budget: compute cost_usd_at_run_time per cell from profile.pricing × token streams
    at close. Accumulate into <out>/budget.json. Halt before next cell when cap hit.
    Skipped cells get final_status=budget_halted placeholder with process_outcome=
    setup_failed and a 'note' field.
  - Per-cell retry: bounded exponential backoff for transient errors (connection
    refused, 5xx, EOF parse). Write attempt_of: link in the new cell; back-write
    superseded_by: into the prior cell (the one allowed mutation of a closed cell).

SCOPE — harbor-runner Docker image:
  - scripts/benchmark/Dockerfile.harbor-runner:
      FROM python:3.12-slim
      RUN pip install --no-cache-dir harbor-bench==<pinned-version>
      COPY scripts/benchmark/harbor_adapters/ /app/harbor_adapters/
      COPY scripts/benchmark/harbor_agent.py /app/harbor_agent.py
      ENV PYTHONPATH=/app
      WORKDIR /app

  - scripts/benchmark/build-harbor-runner.sh: docker build with image-content-sha

SCOPE — shell adapters (8 harness-adapters + 1 task-executor):
  - scripts/benchmark/task-executors/harbor: bash wrapper around
      docker run --rm -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \\
        -v \"\$cell_dir:/output\" -v \"\$tasks_dir:/tasks:ro\" \\

    Reads task-spec.json from stdin (see CONTRACT.md). Writes cell_dir/result.json.

      <name> command (reads profile JSON on stdin) -> command-spec.json on stdout

    The current Python adapters at scripts/benchmark/harness_adapters/{fiz,opencode,

description:
PROBLEM
The routing reliability epic still requires MaxPower to exclude overpowered candidates when an in-bounds route exists. The current scorer only subtracts 1 point per power level above MaxPower, so a power-10 candidate can still beat a power-8 in-bounds candidate through other bonuses. That leaves --max-power as a weak preference instead of a reliable upper bound.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
internal/routing/score.go:266-269 applies only penalty := power - MaxPower for above-max candidates. service_routing.go:219-229 mirrors that weak public PowerHintFit value. Existing tests in internal/routing/score_power_test.go cover soft bounds and provider preference, but there is no TestScorePolicy_MaxPowerExcludesOverpoweredCandidates proving an above-max route cannot win while an in-bounds route is available.

PROPOSED FIX
Make MaxPower an exclusion-strength signal for automatic selection whenever at least one eligible in-bounds candidate exists, while preserving explicit pins and the existing MinPower soft-floor behavior. Add the named regression and adjust score evidence so above-max candidates show the exclusion/penalty clearly.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change MinPower soft-floor semantics. Do not change explicit provider/model pin behavior. Do not add another routing policy path or bead metadata input.

description:
Make the openai-compat provider's reasoning translator consult the
L1→L2→L3 wire-form chain from ADR-010 Amendment 2026-05-11:

  L1: live introspection (from the introspection-adapter bead
      fizeau-e80c156e — read once at provider construction, merged into

  L2: catalog `reasoning_wire` field (from the schema bead

  L3: static ThinkingFormat per provider type (today's behavior)

Per the amendment, this bead also fixes two pre-existing translator bugs
discovered in the 2026-05-11 probing session and adds one new wire format.

Three coordinated changes:

### 1. L1/L2/L3 lookup chain

Signature change: `openRouterReasoningOptions(policy)` becomes
`openRouterReasoningOptions(policy, model, effectiveWire)`. The
`reasoningRequestOptions` caller (around openai.go:340) consults in
order:
  - introspection.SupportedRequestParams + introspection.AliasMap (L1)
  - modelReasoningWireFor(model) (L2)
  - p.thinkingWireFormat() default (L3)
and passes the resolved wire choice into format-specific helpers.

Tier↔tokens conversion via PortableBudgets:
  - caller passed KindNamed, wire wants tokens: PortableBudgets[name]
  - caller passed KindTokens, wire wants tier: snap to nearest
    PortableBudgets tier rounding UP on ties (4096 -> medium because
    4096 is the midpoint of 2048+8192).

### 2. Fix ThinkingWireFormatQwen to use chat_template_kwargs envelope

Verified 2026-05-11 against sindri-llamacpp: top-level enable_thinking
is silently dropped (4 completion tokens, no reasoning). The
chat_template_kwargs envelope variant produces 250-526 tokens with
reasoning extracted.

The current code at openai.go:421-425 emits:
  option.WithJSONSet(\"enable_thinking\", true)
  option.WithJSONSet(\"thinking_budget\", thinkingBudget)

The new code must emit:

description:
Two-failure pattern from 2026-05-10 sweeps where a single misconfigured lane wasted significant compute before any human noticed:

(1) sindri-llamacpp lane: profile had `reasoning: low` set, but fiz's llama-server provider rejects that param. Every cell in the lane failed in ~47s with the same `agent: provider error: openai: reasoning="low" is not supported by provider type "llama-server"` error. The matrix runner kept marching through all 89 tasks × 3 reps without bailing. Caught after 119 cells (~93 minutes of churn).

(2) sindri-vllm lane (same evening): the vLLM model server entered a degraded state where /v1/models responded but /v1/chat/completions hung indefinitely. Each cell wasted its full agent budget (~45 min) waiting for a single llm.request that never produced an llm.response.

Common shape: same misconfiguration / failure causing every cell in a lane to fail identically. Today there's no mechanism to detect "this lane is not going to work, stop trying."

Two child beads address this in priority order:

description:
PROBLEM
The claude batch adapter and claude-tui PTY adapter can fail for different runtime reasons, but neither currently preserves reliable typed failure evidence from the surface that actually executed. The 2026-07-14 batch incident returned exit status 1 while stderr said Failed to authenticate and Could not refresh auth token. Fizeau therefore lost the dispatchability cause and exact surface identity needed for bounded route feedback. A host account probe, a live TUI process, and a fresh batch process are separate evidence sources and must never poison one another.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
internal/harnesses/claude/runner.go prefers runErr.Error over non-empty stderr, collapsing diagnostics to exit status 1. internal/harnesses/claude-tui/harness.go has a small fatal-screen marker table and generic final messages but no typed RoutingActual failure class. internal/serviceimpl/execute_subprocess.go fills routing identity only when RoutingActual is nil, so adapter-owned FailureClass cannot be safely combined with the service-resolved route tuple. CONTRACT-003 exposes failure_class but does not define its stable vocabulary or semantics.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a shared classifier under internal/harnesses/anthropic for execution-time Claude diagnostics. Its stable classes are credential_invalid, quota_exhausted, transport, protocol, and unknown. Precedence is quota markers, including credit-balance exhaustion, then authentication or credential markers including HTTP 401, then transport, then generic protocol, then unknown. Preserve a bounded sanitized diagnostic of at most 2048 bytes; redact bearer and API tokens, refresh tokens, and account identifiers. The batch adapter may preserve sanitized stderr alongside the process error. The TUI adapter may preserve only matched fatal lines, never the full rendered frame or prompt. Both adapters attach the class and their own harness identity before terminal delivery. Service stamping makes the resolved Harness, Provider, ServerInstance, and Model authoritative even over conflicting adapter identity, while preserving adapter-owned FailureClass. Document the vocabulary in CONTRACT-003. Sister bead fizeau-80dcedde owns exactly-once observation, route-health admission, and cooldown.

NON-SCOPE
Do not run claude auth status as a universal truth source, expose credentials or account identifiers, infer that a sibling Claude surface failed, declare host login state, make DDx parse text or choose a harness, change default routing, change route scoring, record route health, or change generic terminal-delivery ordering.

PARENT
fizeau-6f9ffa71.

DEPENDENCY
fizeau-80dcedde consumes this typed surface evidence and must remain blocked on this bead.

description:
PROBLEM

DDx executions routed through Fizeau v0.15.2 claude-tui exit before a Claude turn starts. Two Niflheim attempts on 2026-07-23 failed after 10.784s and 2.612s with Claude TUI PTY closed before Stop hook; one reported exit status unavailable and one exit code 143. A bounded smoke reproduction with Claude Code 2.1.218 failed twice in 3.870s and 5.698s with zero tokens, empty output, and no Stop payload. DDx later observed and reaped the provider process in the historical attempts; that cleanup is downstream evidence, not the origin of the failure.

REPRODUCTION

Run:

ddx --no-update-check run --harness claude-tui --model sonnet-4.6 --permissions unrestricted --timeout 30s --output session-jsonl --text Diagnostic-smoke-test-only-reply-CLAUDE_TUI_REPRO_OK

Observed service sessions svc-1784850966893529128 and svc-1784851045525081838 fail with cause=harness_failed and Claude TUI PTY closed before Stop hook. Directly launching Claude Code 2.1.218 under a PTY with either --permission-mode bypassPermissions or --dangerously-skip-permissions displays a mandatory choice with the cursor on 1. No, exit and option 2. Yes, I accept. Sending Enter exits code 1 immediately and reproduces the zero-token, empty-output, no-Stop pattern.

ROOT CAUSE

internal/harnesses/claude-tui/harness.go:1452-1492 models every interstitial as dismissible with a default-accept Enter and explicitly assumes the bypass warning defaults to I accept. The turn loop at harness.go:589-595 recognizes the current bypass-warning markers and calls SendKey Enter once. Claude Code 2.1.218 now renders a two-choice bypass consent screen whose default is No, exit, so that Enter terminates Claude before Fizeau sends the task. The subsequent PTY EOF at harness.go:541-570 and absent Stop hook are downstream symptoms. internal/harnesses/claude-tui/runturn_test.go:1148-1205 encodes the obsolete single-action fixture I accept the risk, Press Enter to continue, so the regression remains green.

The captured current screen says WARNING: Claude Code running in Bypass Permissions mode, explains the risk, then renders cursor-selected 1. No, exit, 2. Yes, I accept, and Enter to confirm. Both permission flag forms show it on Claude Code 2.1.218.

PROPOSED FIX

Make bypass-consent handling selection-aware. Treat it as a distinct elevated-permission decision, not a generic Enter-dismissed interstitial. If the request carries explicit unrestricted authorization, deliberately select Yes, I accept, confirm, wait for the normal ready prompt, then deliver the task. Without explicit authorization, fail before task injection with a typed, sanitized preflight or configuration diagnostic. Do not silently persist operator consent. Preserve a bounded sanitized startup-screen classification in the final diagnostic so future CLI UI drift does not collapse into generic PTY EOF.

NON-SCOPE

Do not change DDx provider-child cleanup, weaken Stop-hook nonce validation, infer success without a Stop payload, or replace claude-tui with the headless Claude adapter.

description:
fiz retries transient provider errors (connection refused, EOF, 5xx) internally up to ~5 times with exponential backoff. Each retry attempt counts as a turn in the matrix, inflating the turns counter even when zero useful work happened. Result: cells where the provider was completely unreachable end up with turns=6 (5 retries), output_tokens=0, terminated_mid_work=nil, but `matrixHasMeaningfulAttempt(report)` returns true because turns > 0 — bypassing the new invalid_provider classifier rule introduced in 6688326e (fizeau-e874633d).

Concrete incident: on 2026-05-11 ~15:25Z, vidar:1235 oMLX server crashed. 70 cells silently failed before detection. fiz.txt showed:
  2026/05/11 15:29:41 WARN provider error, retrying attempt=1 err="unexpected EOF"
  2026/05/11 15:29:42 WARN provider error, retrying attempt=2 err="connect: connection refused"
  ... etc through attempt=5
Each cell ended with turns=6, wall=60-200s, final_status=graded_fail. Classifier left them as plain graded_fail — i.e. "the model attempted and failed" — polluting vidar's pass-rate denominator with what was actually 100% provider unavailability.

The hole is structural: hasMeaningfulAttempt currently looks at turns/tokens/tool_calls > 0. fiz's retry counter is one of the inputs to that signal, but a retry isn't a meaningful attempt — it's the absence of one.

PROPOSED FIX

Add a stronger "no real attempt" signal that distinguishes retry-spam from real turns. Two complementary options:

A. **fiz records retry attempts separately** from successful llm.request/response pairs. The session jsonl would carry an `llm.retry` event (or annotate llm.request with an `attempt` field). The matrix runner already reads the session jsonl in readSessionSignalsFromCell — it can extend the count to distinguish "had_completed_response" from "had_request". Then: graded_fail + !had_completed_response + had_request → invalid_provider, regardless of turns count.

B. **Token-based fallback in the existing classifier**: even if turns > 0, if input_tokens=0 AND output_tokens=0 AND had_llm_request=true AND tmw=nil, classify as invalid_provider. The intuition: a real turn consumes prompt tokens (input_tokens > 0 from session.end usage). All-zero token counts means no completed round-trip ever happened. Cheaper than (A) but a bit more heuristic.

In-scope files for Part B (simpler, ships first):
- cmd/bench/matrix_invalid.go — extend the case "graded_fail" branch with the token-based check before the !hasAttempt branch.
- cmd/bench/matrix_invalid_test.go — fixture: graded-fail-retry-spam.json with turns=6, input_tokens=0, output_tokens=0, had_llm_request=true, tmw=nil → expects invalid_provider.
- scripts/benchmark/reclassify-invalid.py — mirror.
- Run reclassifier; expect ~70+ historical vidar cells from 2026-05-11 to flip invalid_setup/empty → invalid_provider.

In-scope for Part A (deeper, file as separate bead if simple fix isn't enough):
- internal/core/loop.go — distinguish "request attempted but provider error retried" from "completed request/response pair" in event emission. Add an `attempt` field on llm.request or a new event type.
- scripts/benchmark/harbor_agent.py FizeauAgent.parse_telemetry — count completed responses (not just requests) when populating turns/tokens fields.
- cmd/bench/matrix.go readSessionSignalsFromCell — return n_completed_responses alongside the existing tmw/had_llm_request signals.

ACCEPTANCE IS A COMMAND

1. go test ./cmd/bench/... -run TestClassifyMatrixInvalid passes with the new fixture graded-fail-retry-spam.json asserting invalid_provider.
2. .venv-report/bin/python scripts/benchmark/reclassify-invalid.py --dry-run flags the cells from the 2026-05-11 vidar incident (70+ cells) as transitioning to invalid_provider.
3. Apply pass leaves those cells excluded from vidar's pass-rate denominator and tagged for --retry-invalid reruns.

WHY THIS MATTERS

Without this, every server-side outage (oMLX crash, vLLM hang, network blip) gets attributed to model quality instead of provider availability. Pass@k denominators include hundreds of cells where the model never actually got to try. The defense-in-depth piece (fizeau-72d18004 consecutive-failure halt in the matrix runner) catches this at sweep-execution time, but classification matters even retroactively for accurate reporting.
title: bench: classifier misses retry-spam cells (turns inflated by fiz internal retries on connection errors)

description:
PROBLEM: ModelDiscoveryHarness.DefaultModelSnapshot() for claude-tui must be derived from live PTY observation of the Anthropic CLI. The no-static-fallback principle (fizeau-89eca738) forbids any Go-literal ModelSnapshot fallback in production code; on PTY failure the method must return ErrModelDiscoveryEvidenceMissing, never a baked snapshot.

ROOT CAUSE:
- Other harnesses currently embed Go-literal snapshots as a convenience; reusing that pattern in claude-tui would violate fizeau-89eca738.
- The ModelDiscoveryHarness contract requires a fresh, CLI-derived snapshot, not a constant.
- Without an AST/static check, future contributors could silently reintroduce a literal snapshot fallback.
- Cassettes under testdata/ are valid for test fixtures only; loading them from production code paths would also violate the principle.

PROPOSED FIX:
1. Implement claudetui.Harness.DefaultModelSnapshot(): spawn a /model (or equivalent) PTY query against the live CLI, parse the output via internal/harnesses/anthropic helpers, return a harnesses.ModelSnapshot.
2. On PTY error, unparseable output, or empty result, return a sentinel ErrModelDiscoveryEvidenceMissing. Do not fall back to any literal.
3. Restrict cassette usage to *_test.go files; production source must not reference testdata/ paths.
4. Add a build-time or test-time static analyzer that scans the claudetui package AST for any composite literal of type ModelSnapshot (or its fields) outside *_test.go and fails the build if found.

description:
PROBLEM
The credit probe in [[openrouter-credit-balance-probe-and-cache]] can fail in two distinct ways that operators need to distinguish:
- 401 from `/api/v1/credits` → the key is set but rejected (e.g. revoked, typo'd). This is different from "never set a key" because the fix is different (rotate vs configure).
- Transport failure (DNS, TCP, TLS, 5xx) → openrouter.ai is unreachable. This is transient and we must not hard-exclude openrouter forever, or one bad minute permanently demotes the provider.

Without this distinction operators cannot triage; without fail-open recovery a transient blip causes flapping or sustained mis-routing.

ROOT CAUSE
The probe path introduced by [[openrouter-credit-balance-probe-and-cache]] needs explicit failure-classification branches and a freshness-window policy. The error handling for the openrouter credits roundtripper response must inspect status code and error type, then write a typed `filter_reason` into the cache rather than a generic error string. Exact integration point: the cache-write call in the credit-probe routine.

PROPOSED FIX
1. **401 from /credits** → cache `filter_reason: "credential_invalid"` (distinct from `"credential_missing"` emitted by [[openrouter-credential-presence-gate]]). Candidate `eligible: false`. Operators reading routing_decision can tell "forgot to set" from "key rejected".
2. **Transport error / non-401 5xx** → cache `filter_reason: "provider_unreachable"`. Candidate `eligible: false` for the current freshness window ONLY — do not hard-exclude. Next scheduled probe pass attempts a fresh call; on success the candidate returns to `eligible: true` automatically.
3. **Fail-open semantics**: a `provider_unreachable` cache entry must NOT be sticky beyond the probe interval. After the next probe attempt the cache reflects the new state (success or another failure-class). No manual operator intervention required to recover.
4. **Evidence in routing_decision**: each filter_reason carries the originating HTTP status code (or transport error class) in the candidate evidence body so the operator does not have to grep logs.

NON-SCOPE
- Credential presence/format checks (handled by [[openrouter-credential-presence-gate]]).
- The credit balance probe and its caching layer itself (handled by [[openrouter-credit-balance-probe-and-cache]]).
- Retry-with-backoff against openrouter.ai on transport failure during the probe — the probe is best-effort; the next scheduled pass is the retry.
- Multi-account credential rotation / failover (parent non-scope, preserved).
- Per-model credit-cost forecasting (parent non-scope, preserved).
- DDx-side changes per CONTRACT-003 (parent non-scope, preserved).

CROSS-REF
Sibling beads: [[openrouter-credential-presence-gate]], [[openrouter-credit-balance-probe-and-cache]]. Cross-ref fizeau-80d4bf41.
title: openrouter: probe failure-mode handling (credential_invalid vs provider_unreachable, fail-open recovery)

description:
GOAL
Fizeau's auto-router must reliably select an executable route whenever ANY configured provider is reachable and within quota. Today the drain stalls or routes to dead hosts even when subscription/cloud providers are healthy. Caller (DDx) should receive provider_connectivity / no_viable_provider ONLY when literally every configured provider is unavailable.

OBSERVED FAILURE MODES (from a 27-bead harness-interface refactor drain on 2026-05-14)
1. Policy-scoring disabled under bounds. When --min-power or --max-power is set, internal/routing/score.go:60 and :108 skip the policy-aware preference block entirely. A free subscription candidate at the floor power loses to a metered candidate at higher power purely due to the absent policy bonus. Tracked in child bead fizeau-dc3cf359.

2. Dead-host route loop without cross-provider escalation. When the smart-routing scorer ranks fiz/bragi/qwen3.5-27b above claude/claude-sonnet-4-6 (because the default-policy local-deployment bias is winning), and bragi is unreachable, the request fails after exhausting bragi's ports (1234, 8020) and grendel's ports (1234, 1235, 8000) within a single bead-attempt, then errors with provider_connectivity — even though claude/claude-sonnet-4-6 is sitting at score 186 in fiz route-status. Cross-provider escalation needs to fall through to subscription/cloud once local providers fail.

3. Cross-process route-health amnesia. Each new ddx-try process spawns a fresh in-process routehealth.Store. Bragi being unreachable was learned by the previous attempt and persisted into the bead's work-failed-routes (via fizeau-8134d6db + ddx-71629938), but the *next* bead's first dial still goes to bragi for 5s before falling back. Aggregate cost: ~10–20s of dial timeouts per fresh ddx-try. Tracked separately in fizeau-7cd66e6b (pending ADR-012 carve-out decision).

4. Score for the same candidate varies wildly between bounded and unbounded queries. fiz route-status shows claude/claude-sonnet-4-6 at score 186 (no bounds, default policy); the same candidate scores ~110 with --min-power 8. That delta is the missing policy bonus. Tracked in fizeau-dc3cf359.

CONTRACT (what 'reliable' means)
- Given a healthy provider configured in fizeau.config.yaml — local OR subscription OR openrouter — and a request without an explicit provider pin, the router MUST select a route that succeeds. Provider liveness is determined by route-health signal + first-attempt dial.
- Caller-supplied --harness, --min-power, --max-power constraints MUST NOT cause systematic preference for more-expensive in-bounds candidates over cheaper-but-equally-eligible ones.
- Once a provider has been observed unreachable in the current ddx-try attempt's per-request route exclusion list, the router MUST NOT re-attempt that provider until the exclusion expires or the worker is restarted.
- If literally every configured provider is unreachable AND every subscription provider has zero quota AND no cloud route is reachable, the router emits no_viable_provider and the caller can decide.
- The router MUST emit a clear routing-decision evidence event naming each candidate scored, why it was selected or rejected, and the final decision — so operators can audit 'why did it pick X over Y'.

SCOPE
- Fix the policy-scoring-under-bounds bug (fizeau-dc3cf359) — surgical change to internal/routing/score.go.
- Add an integration test: with bragi unreachable (mock dial-failing endpoint), a smart-policy request lands on claude (subscription) within one routing decision, no per-bead 30s timeout.
- Add an integration test: with --min-power 8, default-policy request picks the free-subscription candidate over the metered candidate at the same power.
- Add an integration test: with all configured providers dial-failing, the router returns no_viable_provider in under 2× per-attempt dial timeout (not 5× or more).
- Document the routing contract in docs/helix/02-design/contracts/CONTRACT-003 §Routing (or a new section) so callers can rely on it.

NON-SCOPE
- Route-health cross-process persistence (fizeau-7cd66e6b is its own bead; depends on ADR-012 carve-out decision).
- Cooldown policy changes (ddx-side bead ddx-63688d7b owns that).
- Connect-timeout tuning (fizeau-b5757624 already shipped).
- Provider config schema changes.

DEPS
- Decompose into child beads if scope exceeds 5 ACs / 500 lines / 5 unrelated files. Otherwise treat as one focused fix touching internal/routing/score.go + service_routing.go projection + tests.

CHILDREN
- fizeau-dc3cf359 (policy-scoring-under-bounds; surgical)
notes: Closed after child beads fizeau-dc3cf359, fizeau-126f03c0, fizeau-f79d434b, fizeau-f02ada30, fizeau-a77e62b6, and fizeau-ce4216aa landed. Local verification: go test ./... -count=1 passed; go test ./internal/routing/... ./... -count=1 passed; targeted routing tests for dead-local fallback, all-dead fail-fast, min/max power scoring, and raw score components passed. CONTRACT-003, FEAT-004, SD-005, ADR-012, and CHANGELOG now describe cache-first route hot paths and score evidence.
title: routing: complete reliability — succeed against any available provider, fail only when no providers remain

description:
PROBLEM: The metered native claude transport under-counts actual_cash_spend when prompt caching is active. nativeCostUSD (internal/harnesses/claude/native_runner.go:270) computes cost via agentcore.DefaultPricing.EstimateCost(model, u.Input, u.Output) — input+output tokens ONLY. agentcore.TokenUsage (internal/core/agent.go:46) carries CacheRead and CacheWrite token counts, and ModelPricing (internal/core/pricing.go:9-10) carries CacheReadPerM/CacheWritePerM rates, but EstimateCost (internal/core/pricing.go:37) ignores both. So a cached turn is billed too low.

ROOT CAUSE: internal/core/pricing.go:37 EstimateCost(model, inputTokens, outputTokens) has no cache params; nativeCostUSD passes only u.Input/u.Output, dropping u.CacheRead/u.CacheWrite.

PROPOSED FIX: Add a cache-aware method PricingTable.EstimateCostWithCache(model string, input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite int) float64 returning the input+output cost PLUS float64(cacheRead)/1e6*CacheReadPerM + float64(cacheWrite)/1e6*CacheWritePerM, keeping the same unknown-model contract (return -1 for unknown model). Prefer a NEW method (do NOT change EstimateCost's signature — other callers depend on it). Update nativeCostUSD (native_runner.go:270) to call the new method with u.CacheRead/u.CacheWrite, preserving the existing negative=>0 guard.

NON-SCOPE: do NOT change the subprocess-path cost (it gets total_cost_usd from the CLI). Do NOT change existing EstimateCost callers. Do NOT flip the default transport.
title: native claude cost: include cache-read/write tokens in metered CostUSD

description:
Two CI gates lock in the contract:

(a) Cassette-as-test-fixture freshness (every PR): every harness with a TUI model surface (codex, claude, gemini, opencode, pi) has testdata/model_surface/ checked in and CapturedAt within a configured TTL (default 30 days). Stale fixtures fail because they no longer prove the parser works against current TUI output.

(b) Live-discovery drift detector (scheduled / credentialed, harness_integration tag): runs ReadXModelDiscoveryViaPTY against the live authenticated CLI, captures a fresh snapshot, diffs against the checked-in cassette. Mismatch fails with a re-record instruction. Missing credentials emit a structured SKIP (parsable by CI). SKIPs older than TTL fail the presence check above.

This is now scoped correctly: at runtime, live PTY is authoritative and uncached cassette has no role. The CI gates here exist to keep test fixtures honest, not to gate runtime behaviour.
title: harness: CI gate — cassette presence + freshness + credentialed drift detector

## Aggregation

p50 latency comes from a sliding-window in-memory counter (recent N
requests per provider). On crash/restart, signal is reset (cache file

short-TTL by design.

## Cache integration

Each provider gets its own `runtime/<provider>.json` file in M1's
cache. 5-minute TTL. Stale-while-revalidate: snapshot reads return
immediately, background refresh fires.

description:
Follow-on epic for the approved routing plan from 2026-05-13.

End state: every unpinned autorouting decision is a pure function of client inputs plus the current fiz models snapshot. The snapshot is the single source of routing facts: health, quota, model availability, context/tools/reasoning support, billing kind, effective cost, actual-cash-spend flag, locality, reliability, latency, utilization, and freshness. Route code must not maintain a second hidden provider-probe path.

Freshness is a fiz contract, not a required fiz daemon. Fiz provides synchronous refresh APIs/CLI behavior with cross-process locks, single-flight/coalescing, TTLs, cooldowns, and atomic snapshot writes. Autorouting can synchronously refresh stale routing-relevant fields before scoring. CLI commands must not create refresh storms. fiz models is quick and reads the snapshot; if stale fields exist it prints clear refresh guidance rather than launching uncoordinated background probes. Foreground --refresh and --refresh-all are available for serverless operation.

Fiz also exposes an optional async refresh/warmup mechanism that an external long-lived owner such as ddx server can call on a heartbeat to maintain freshness. That async maintainer is an optimization only; route correctness must not depend on ddx server integration.

Routing gates only on true constraints or dispatchability: pins, no_remote, metered actual-spend refusal, required tools/context/reasoning, known down endpoints, quota exhaustion, and pin conflicts. Everything else is scoring. Subscription-backed models use PAYG-equivalent shadow/effective cost for scoring, with actual_cash_spend=false, so cheap naturally prefers nano/mini/local over GPT-5.5 without policy-specific exclusion gates.

Closes when child beads specify, implement, and verify: specs, snapshot schema, coordinated refresh, CLI refresh behavior, routing purity, effective-cost scoring, and route traceability.

description:
Add `fiz models` as a top-level CLI subcommand. Default view shows
the assembled snapshot from M2; flags filter and refresh. Detail view
via `fiz models <ref>` with shortform fuzzy resolution per ADR-012's
naming convention.

Also updates FEAT-006 (standalone CLI) doc to register the new
subcommand and document the interface.

## CLI surface

```
fiz models [flags]                     # list view
fiz models <ref> [flags]               # detail view
fiz cache prune                        # related cache GC
```

## Flags (list view)

- `--refresh`         Force-refresh all sources synchronously before showing
- `--no-refresh`      Don't trigger background refresh on stale data
- `--json`            Machine-readable output
- `--provider <name>` Filter to one provider
- `--power-min <n>`   Filter Power >= n
- `--power-max <n>`   Filter Power <= n
- `--include-noise`   Show low-power, unranked, deprecated entries
  (default suppresses to keep output clean)

## Default filter rules (suppress noise)

- Within (family, tier): keep top 2 versions (current + previous)
- Drop entries with Power < 3 (noise)
- Drop entries with Tier == TierUnknown AND Power == 0
- Show AutoRoutable=false but mark them clearly

`--include-noise` shows everything (useful for debugging the
snapshot, OR's long tail, etc.)

## Detail view (`fiz models <ref>`)

Resolution per ADR-012:
- Full canonical (`<provider>/<id>`) → exact lookup
- Shortform (no `/`) → search snapshot:
  - Exactly one match: use it
  - Multiple matches: list candidates with full canonical IDs, exit 1
  - No matches: show fuzzy-match suggestions, exit 1

Detail output: full KnownModel struct + raw discovery data + full
catalog entry + recent runtime signals + AutoRoutable composition
breakdown (which factor blocked, if any).

## Output format (default)

Tabular, columns: PROVIDER MODEL FAMILY VERSION TIER POWER COST/M
STATUS QUOTA AUTO

Color: AutoRoutable=true green, =false dim. Pre-release in italics.
Status colored (Available green, RateLimited yellow, Unreachable red).

`--json` emits the snapshot serialized as JSON.

## In-scope files

- cmd/fiz/models.go — subcommand registration
- cmd/fiz/models_list.go — list view + filters
- cmd/fiz/models_detail.go — detail view + resolution
- cmd/fiz/models_test.go
- cmd/fiz/cache_prune.go — `fiz cache prune` subcommand
- docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-006-standalone-cli.md — register
  `fiz models` and `fiz cache prune` subcommands; document flags

## Depends on

- M0 (ADR-012) accepted
- M2 (snapshot assembler)
- M3 (runtime signals)

## Out of scope

- Routing's consumption of the snapshot (handled in routing-layer
  beads downstream; this bead is the operator UI)
- OR sub-provider syntax in resolution (M5 deferred)

description:
PROBLEM
Running `fiz --provider local` (and long bench sessions) leaks orphaned harness subprocesses. Observed 2026-05-27 on the dev host: 366 leaked `gemini` node processes, ~14 GB RSS, accumulated over 15+ hours, all reparented to PID 1 (parents long dead). The same shape applies to any harness whose CLI spawns its own children: on a NORMAL (successful) run the spawned process group is never signaled, so any grandchild the harness CLI itself forked survives fizeau's exit and orphans.

ROOT CAUSE (file:line)
- Every harness runner creates a fresh process group via setProcessGroupAttr (Setpgid=true) in internal/harnesses/{harness}/runner_unix.go and ships a killProcessGroup helper that signals the negative pgid.
- internal/harnesses/gemini/runner.go:274-282 — the cleanup goroutine calls killProcessGroup(cmd) ONLY on `<-ctx.Done()`. On normal completion the `<-stdoutReady` branch wins and the goroutine returns without killing the group. cmd.Wait() (runner.go:286) reaps only the direct child; any process the gemini CLI itself spawned (the gemini main -> gemini worker pairs seen in `ps`) stays in the group, un-signaled, and orphans to PID 1.
- killProcessGroup (internal/harnesses/{harness}/runner_unix.go) sends a single SIGTERM with no SIGKILL escalation, so even on cancel/timeout a child that ignores SIGTERM survives.
- A stale-harness reaper exists (service_stale_harness_reaper.go + service_stale_harness_reaper_unix.go terminateOwnedProcessGroup, SIGTERM->SIGKILL) but NOTHING in the runners registers a harness-sessions/*.json record at cmd.Start(), so the reaper has no PIDs/PGIDs to act on and is effectively a no-op for these leaks.
- Audit the sibling runners for the same conditional-cleanup shape: internal/harnesses/claude/runner.go:263 & :426, internal/harnesses/codex/runner.go:233, internal/harnesses/pi/runner.go:207, internal/harnesses/opencode/runner.go:204 (spawn via internal/harnesses/exec.go:18 HarnessCommand).

PROPOSED FIX
1. Kill the process group on EVERY exit path of every harness runner (success, error, timeout, cancel) — not only on ctx cancellation. e.g. ensure the cleanup goroutine always calls killProcessGroup before the runner returns, or `defer killProcessGroup(cmd)` immediately after a successful Start.
2. Escalate killProcessGroup to SIGTERM -> bounded grace -> SIGKILL (mirror terminateOwnedProcessGroup in service_stale_harness_reaper_unix.go) so stubborn grandchildren cannot survive.
3. Backstop: either register a (pid,pgid) session record at cmd.Start() that the stale-harness reaper consumes, or remove the dead reaper infra and document why. Wire one path so the reaper is not silently inert.

NON-SCOPE
- Harness output parsing/streaming behavior is unchanged.
- Windows process-group semantics (only *_unix.go is covered) — out of scope; note if it matters.
- The claude-tui PTY-pool orphan reaper (fizeau-a14eba0c) is a distinct mechanism; cross-ref only.

CROSS-REF: fizeau-a14eba0c (claude-tui PTY orphan reaper).
title: harnesses: kill the spawned process group on every exit path (not just ctx-cancel) — gemini/claude/codex subprocesses orphan and leak

description:
Add a per-lane preflight check to scripts/benchmark/run_terminalbench_2_1_sweep.sh that fires a single 1-token chat completion against each requested lane's endpoint before any matrix runner spawns. If the endpoint cannot produce a token within 30s using the lane's actual sampling params, fail the sweep with a non-zero exit and a clear message naming the lane, the endpoint, the model id, and the underlying error.

Why this matters: see parent epic. The 2026-05-10 sindri-llamacpp incident wasted 119 cells (~93 min) on a `reasoning: low` parameter the llama-server provider rejects. The same hour, sindri-vllm wasted multiple cells on a hung model engine where /v1/models responded but /v1/chat/completions never streamed tokens. A single curl-to-completion check per lane catches all these classes (plus auth failures, missing-model 404s, connection-refused, wrong content-type) at sweep startup, before any matrix runner spawns.

Behavior:

- Fire after `Resolved tasks:` is printed, before the per-lane "starting" markers.
- For each lane in the resolved plan: build a JSON body using the lane's `fizeau_env.FIZEAU_MODEL` and the lane's sampling block (temperature, top_p, top_k, reasoning when present). POST to `<base_url>/chat/completions` with `max_tokens: 1` and a 30s timeout.
- Pass condition: the response is JSON-parseable and `.choices[0].message.content` is a non-null string (even an empty string is OK — the model started decoding).
- Fail condition: any non-2xx, timeout, malformed JSON, or missing message content. Print the lane id, base_url, model id, sampling params attempted, and the response body (truncated to 1KB).
- Skip preflight for managed-cloud lanes that have always-on SLAs (openrouter, openai, anthropic) — these are well-known and a preflight just burns quota. Identify by checking the resource group's `provider_type` against an allow-list (vllm, llama-server, omlx, lmstudio, rapid-mlx, ollama, lucebox).

- scripts/benchmark/run_terminalbench_2_1_sweep.sh — add preflight_lane() function + per-lane invocation loop right before the existing per-lane plan output.
- scripts/benchmark/terminalbench-2-1-sweep.yaml — no schema change needed; the existing `fizeau_env` and `sampling` blocks are sufficient.

Out-of-scope (file separate beads):

With sindri-llamacpp configured to use `reasoning: low` (the broken state we just fixed), `scripts/benchmark/run_terminalbench_2_1_sweep.sh --phase full --lanes sindri-llamacpp,vidar --dry-run` exits non-zero with `[preflight] sindri-llamacpp FAILED: reasoning="low" is not supported by provider type "llama-server"` (or equivalent error text) and does not print any per-lane "starting" marker.

description:
PROBLEM: CONTRACT-004 always invokes dynamic binaries as ld-linux --library-path <roots> <entrypoint>. For self-image-sensitive standalone ELFs this changes /proc/self/exe and can launch the wrong embedded program: the publisher-authenticated OpenCode 1.3.17 arm64 binary reports/runs Bun 1.3.11 through the current recipe while direct kernel execution reports OpenCode 1.3.17. Shape-only closure success would silently violate execution parity.

PROPOSED FIX: Evolve ADR-014, CONTRACT-003, and CONTRACT-004 with a typed kernel-direct dynamic strategy. The neutral analyzer must bind a bounded deterministic PT_INTERP rewrite from the source ELF to the fixed bundled loader below /opt/fizeau/runtime, retain source and derived digests, and retain exact private library roots. Neutral materialization applies and verifies that transform; activation directly execs the transformed entrypoint with a generated LD_LIBRARY_PATH derived only from typed library-root targets so /proc/self/exe remains the harness binary. Existing explicit-loader recipes remain distinct.

NON-SCOPE: Do not implement OpenCode credential/config/cache discovery, accept an OpenCode release row, change routing/providers, contact a provider, add shell wrappers, use the container base loader/libraries, or weaken value/path redaction.
notes: Rejected after adversarial review: kernel-direct needs LD_LIBRARY_PATH for initial load, which remains in the harness environment and contaminates dynamic child tools; a scratch root would also remove the shell/toolchain the agent needs. This is not a credible v0.15 design. OpenCode 1.3.17 remains fail-closed. Reviewed 1.14.33 is execution-equivalent under existing explicit_loader and will be the recognized release.
title: runtime: preserve ELF self-image in dynamic portable launch

> For a given model power, we need to intelligently choose based on
> "cost", where remaining usage quota impacts the cost.

Cost model (proposed for ADR-011):

- **Subscription with quota remaining**: effective cost ≈ 0 (or
  quota-fraction-aware: lower-cost the more quota remains).
- **Subscription with quota exhausted**: drop from candidates.
- **Per-token API**: effective cost = catalog `cost_input_per_m` ×
  estimated input tokens + `cost_output_per_m` × estimated output
  tokens.
- **Local provider** (free): effective cost = 0 if eligible (per bead
  D's IncludeByDefault filter), else dropped.

Quota signal sources:

- HTTP rate-limit response headers (per recent commit 7776890e —
  `quota_exhausted` already plumbed).
- Subscription `/usage` endpoints when available.
- In-memory recent-rejection rate as fallback.

Quota-pool semantic (from bead E1):

- Models declare a `quota_pool` (defaulting to provider system).
- Pool exhaustion drops all models in that pool from the candidate set.
- Models in a different pool (e.g., `gpt-5.3-codex-spark` in
  `openai-codex-spark`) become eligible as fallbacks even if not
  version-newest, satisfying the "use spark when main pool is empty"
  operator request.

Power-floor semantic:

- Caller / DDx specifies required `MinPower` (and optional `MaxPower`).
- Routing filters candidates to `MinPower ≤ candidate.power ≤ MaxPower`.
- Among survivors, pick min effective cost.
- Tie-break: prefer subscription over PAYG; prefer lower-power if it
  exceeds requirement (cheapest qualified candidate, not most powerful).

## ADR scope

The ADR document itself, written to
`docs/helix/02-design/adr/ADR-011-cost-based-routing-with-quota-pools.md`.
Standard ADR structure: Context, Decision, Consequences, Out of scope,
References.

## Decision points the ADR must resolve

1. Quota fraction → cost mapping (linear? step function? thresholds?).
2. Quota window time handling (do we reserve quota for later? probably
   not in v1 — use available now).
3. Token estimate source (the request itself? a heuristic? a learned
   model?). v1 likely uses a coarse system-prompt-length-based
   estimate.
4. Fallback chain ordering when quota exhausts mid-request (single try?
   retry on alternate?).
5. How `IncludeByDefault: false` (bead D) composes with cost ranking
   (drops from default candidate set entirely; not just deprioritized).

## In-scope files

- docs/helix/02-design/adr/ADR-011-cost-based-routing-with-quota-pools.md
  (new)

## Out of scope

- Implementation (separate EPIC after ADR acceptance).
- Quota signal infrastructure beyond what 7776890e already provides
  (any new signals needed get filed as their own beads under the EPIC).
- Per-tenant or per-key quota tracking (flag as future scope in the
  ADR).

description:
PROBLEM: claude-tui currently has no real turn-execution path; ADR-013 §3 requires driving the Anthropic CLI through internal/pty/ and emitting mid-turn tool_call/tool_result ProgressEvents during the turn (not at Stop), via PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks that coexist with user-defined hooks.

description:
PROBLEM: The claude-tui skeleton from child #1 has no real turn-execution path. ADR-013 §3 requires that claude-tui drive the Anthropic CLI through internal/pty/ and emit intermediate tool_call/tool_result ProgressEvents DURING the turn (not at Stop), via PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks. Subscription billing is observed off the live CLI session, so the wire format must be the interactive PTY surface.

ROOT CAUSE:
- The existing claude harness uses --print and only emits a Final ProgressEvent on subprocess termination; ADR-013 mandates mid-turn events for claude-tui.
- internal/pty/ exists but is not driven by any harness yet; session-pool, /clear-between-turns, and orphan-reaper concerns from ADR-013 are unimplemented for this harness.
- AccountHarness and QuotaHarness need CLI-observed signals (identity, usage) instead of API-metered numbers; existing helpers live in the neutral anthropic/ package after child #1.
- Per testing concern in ADR-013, loop overhead beyond inference must stay under 10ms and wall-time-per-turn must stay within 2x of claude --print on equivalent prompts.

PROPOSED FIX:
1. Implement claudetui.Harness.RunTurn: open or reuse an internal/pty/ session, write the prompt, drive readers, terminate on the CLI's end-of-turn marker, return Final event.
2. Install PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook handlers that emit tool_call and tool_result ProgressEvents on the harness event channel as they fire mid-turn.
3. Implement a session pool keyed by working directory: between turns issue /clear; on shutdown reap any orphaned PTY processes.
4. Resolve hook-conflict concern from ADR-013 by routing claude-tui's hooks through the existing conflict-arbitration layer (no new mechanism).
5. Implement AccountHarness.Identity off CLI auth status output (parsed via anthropic/ helpers).
6. Implement QuotaHarness.Quota off CLI quota observation surface (parsed via anthropic/ helpers).
7. Add a benchmark that compares per-turn wall time against a claude --print baseline on a shared canned prompt and asserts the ratchet.

NON-SCOPE:
- ModelDiscoveryHarness implementation and no-static-fallback enforcement (child #3).
- Capability baseline rows, evidence IDs, ADR-013 status promotion (child #4).
- Cassette-driven static fallback for production code (forbidden by fizeau-89eca738).
- Service-side changes beyond what child #1 already wired.
- Redesigning the hook-conflict arbitration layer; reuse existing infrastructure.

Depends on child #1. Governing artifacts: ADR-013 §3, CONTRACT-004, internal/pty/ library.

description:
Amend the routing and snapshot governing docs so implementation is not relying on chat context.

Required design contract:
- Autorouting decision = route(client_inputs, fiz_models_snapshot).
- Client inputs include policy/profile, pins, no_remote, metered opt-in, tools/context/reasoning needs, and other explicit constraints.
- The fiz models snapshot is the only source of routing facts: health, quota, model availability, effective cost, actual_cash_spend, billing kind, context/tools/reasoning support, locality, reliability, latency, utilization, and per-field freshness.
- Fiz owns synchronous freshness: refresh operations use cross-process locks, single-flight/coalescing, TTLs, cooldowns, bounded concurrency, and atomic snapshot writes. Autorouting may synchronously refresh stale routing-relevant fields before scoring.
- Fiz exposes an optional async refresh/warmup entrypoint that a long-lived ddx server can call on a heartbeat. This is a cache-warming optimization; route correctness must not require ddx server.
- fiz models is quick; it reads the current snapshot and, when fields are stale, prints refresh guidance instead of starting an uncoordinated background probe. fiz models --refresh blocks on routing-relevant stale fields; fiz models --refresh-all blocks on all refreshable fields.
- Hard gates are limited to explicit user constraints and dispatchability. Cost, quality, health risk, latency, utilization, and power fit are scoring inputs.
- Subscription models use PAYG-equivalent effective/shadow cost for scoring while retaining actual_cash_spend=false. Pay-per-token providers are gated only when dispatch creates actual metered spend and the user has not opted in.

In scope: docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-004-model-routing.md, docs/helix/02-design/adr/ADR-011-cost-based-routing-with-quota-pools.md, docs/helix/02-design/contracts/CONTRACT-003-fizeau-service.md, docs/routing/*.md, ADR-012 snapshot/cache docs if present.

Out of scope: implementation code; create follow-up beads instead of partially implementing.
title: Specify snapshot-first autorouting and freshness ownership
