description:
## Problem

Projects that include .ddx/executions/ in their .gitignore (including fizeau and
any repo using the standard DDx .gitignore template) silently fail to land any bead.
The failure is invisible: the implementation is correct, tests pass, but agent.Land()
preserves instead of landing on every attempt.

## Root Cause

cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:701 — RealLandingGitOps.StageDir:

  args := append([]string{"add", "--", relPath}, EvidenceLandExcludePathspecs()...)
  out, err := internalgit.Command(context.Background(), dir, args...).CombinedOutput()

git add without --force silently skips gitignored paths (exit 0, no output, no error).
When .ddx/executions/ is gitignored, StageDir stages nothing. CommitStaged sees an
empty index and returns sha="". landEvidence calls evidenceDirHasTrackedFiles which
also returns false (gitignored files not tracked), so it returns error:
"no staged evidence files under .ddx/executions/...". preserveAfterEvidenceFailure
fires, rolls back master, and creates a preserve ref.

Compounding issue: ApplyLandResultToExecuteBeadResult maps ALL non-pre-merge-check
preserve reasons (including "evidence commit failed") to reasonForStatus="merge
conflict", which ClassifyExecuteBeadStatus returns as "land_conflict" (escalatable).
This causes runEscalatingSingleTierAttempts to burn through the entire model escalation
ladder (min_power 5→7→8→9) before exhausting.

Confirmed in fizeau-bd5193ca: all 4 attempts preserved by evidence commit failure.
Investigation: .ddx/executions/20260510T023250-da87c8c9/fizeau-bd5193ca-investigation.md

## Proposed Fix

Part 1 (fix): In cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:701, StageDir, change:
  args := append([]string{"add", "--", relPath}, ...)
to:
  args := append([]string{"add", "--force", "--", relPath}, ...)

Evidence files are DDx infrastructure, not user source. They must be committed even
when the project's .gitignore covers .ddx/executions/.

Part 2 (defensive): In execute_bead_status.go, add "evidence commit failed:" as a
non-escalatable prefix in isPreservedNeedsReviewReason so infrastructure failures do
not burn the escalation ladder. Fixing Part 1 eliminates the failure path; Part 2
prevents wasted escalation if any other evidence-commit edge case arises.
execute-loop-last-detail: bead misfiled — target source files do not exist in this repository ## Summary This bead (fizeau-af9d5f1c) is filed in the fizeau bead queue, but the changes it prescribes belong to the DDx CLI repository (github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/ddx), not to fizeau (github.com/easel/fizeau). An operator must move/refile the bead into the DDx repo's queue, or explicitly redirect it to patch the vendored skill snapshot under `.agents/skills/cli/` here in fizeau. ## Evidence 1. This worktree's `go.mod` declares `module github.com/easel/fizeau`. There is no top-level `cli/` directory: $ ls cli ls: cannot access 'cli': No such file or directory 2. The bead names `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:701` and `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_status.go`. Neither path exists at the repository root. The only copies present in this repo are read-only skill-bundle mirrors: ./.agents/skills/cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go ./.agents/skills/cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_status.go ./.claude/skills/cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go ./.claude/skills/cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_status.go These are vendored snapshots of the DDx CLI source distributed with the DDx skills package; their `go.mod` says `module github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/ddx`. They were last touched by commit `d49a2428 chore: checkpoint pre-execute-bead 20260508T205324-8992c1f5`, which is a generic checkpoint rather than feature work — consistent with them being a refresh-from-upstream artifact, not a maintenance target. 3. The acceptance criteria assume the DDx repo layout: AC1/AC2: `cd cli && go test -run … ./internal/agent/...` AC3:     `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/...` `cd cli` is not satisfiable here. The closest analogue (`cd .agents/skills/cli && go test ./internal/agent/...`) builds, but it tests vendored upstream code that fizeau does not run — fizeau invokes the `ddx` binary from PATH. Patching the vendored snapshot would not alter the behavior of the installed `ddx` binary that triggers the bug. 4. Patching the vendored snapshot would also be undone the next time the fizeau repo refreshes its skills bundle from upstream DDx, so any local change there is non-durable by design. 5. The bug itself is real and well-diagnosed (fizeau's `.gitignore` does contain `.ddx/executions/`, confirmed at line 28 of `.gitignore`). It is simply that fizeau is the *consumer* exposed by the bug, while the *fix site* is upstream DDx. ## What an operator needs to do Either: - **(preferred)** Recreate this bead in the DDx CLI repository's bead queue with the same title/description/AC, then close fizeau-af9d5f1c with a pointer to the relocated bead; or - **(only if intentional)** Amend the bead description and AC to specify patching `.agents/skills/cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go` and `.agents/skills/cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_status.go` here, replace `cd cli` with `cd .agents/skills/cli` in the AC, and acknowledge in the bead that the patch will be overwritten on the next skills refresh from upstream and therefore needs to be mirrored upstream regardless. Without one of these operator decisions, an agent has no scope-legal way to satisfy this bead in the fizeau worktree. ## Why `proposed` and not `open` The blocker is not retryable by re-running an agent: the source files the bead prescribes are not in this repository, and that condition will not change between attempts. A higher-power model would reach the same dead end. Only an operator can refile or rescope the bead.

## Current state

- `internal/harnesses/registry.go` embeds model discovery snapshots for Codex and Claude.
- `internal/harnesses/types.go` defines `ModelDiscoverySnapshot` with `Models []string`, `ReasoningLevels []string`, and `FreshnessWindow`.

## Problem

Codex and Claude runner defaults are still hardcoded. Adding a newer auto-routable model should require only discovery/catalog evidence, not another runner code edit.

## Scope

1. Add an in-process discovery snapshot cache in `internal/harnesses/discovery_cache.go`, keyed by harness name and snapshot source. For this bead, the source is the embedded cassette snapshot already present in the registry; no live PTY refresh is required.

When no operator `--model` pin is provided, each runner loads the cached snapshot, filters `snapshot.Models` through `Catalog.ModelEligibility(modelID)`, keeps only `AutoRoutable == true`, sorts same-family candidates with `modelcatalog.Parse(...).Compare(...)`, and chooses the highest-ranked candidate.

5. Surface a structured runner/default-resolution signal when the resolved default differs from the prior hardcoded default, so operators can see when discovery changes the selected model.

- Codex explicit `--model gpt-5.4` remains `gpt-5.4`.

type Tier int

description:
PROBLEM: A bash sweep must safely run cells in parallel, survive SIGINT/SIGTERM without orphaning Docker containers or leaving half-owned state, and stop before exceeding a cost cap.

ROOT CAUSE: The A3 runner core executes cells but has no concurrency control, no signal trap, no in-flight accounting, and no budget accumulator; the legacy Go runner's equivalents in cmd/bench/matrix.go are being retired.

PROPOSED FIX (extends scripts/benchmark/benchmark):
- Concurrency: flock per concurrency-group at ${FIZEAU_BENCH_STATE_DIR:-${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/fizeau-benchmark}/locks/<group>.lock; setsid for each cell process group; background-job pool capped by --jobs.
- Signals: trap SIGINT/SIGTERM -> stop accepting new cells; SIGTERM each in-flight cell's process group and `docker stop` each in-flight harbor-runner container; wait 30s then SIGKILL; write final_status=interrupted (process_outcome=killed, no metrics) to in-flight cells; exit non-zero.
- In-flight state: ${FIZEAU_BENCH_STATE_DIR}/<hostname>/in-flight.json; under flock append this cell at start, read current count into the cell, remove at close; prune stale entries (dead PID) at next read.
- Budget: compute cost_usd_at_run_time per cell from profile.pricing × token streams at close; accumulate into <out>/budget.json; halt before the next cell when the cap is hit; skipped cells get final_status=budget_halted placeholder with process_outcome=setup_failed and a 'note' field.

NON-SCOPE: runner dispatch/matrix/--plan/execution loop (A3, prerequisite); harbor image (A1); shell adapters (A2); Go agent-leak fix, parity, deactivation (A5); plus parent out-of-scope: cell-report.schema.json (PR B), tasks_from/task_executor schema (PR C), Node collector (PR D), Node importers (PR E), deleting cmd/bench (PR F), docs (PR G).

GOVERNING ARTIFACT: plan-2026-05-15-benchmark-runner-simplification.

DEPENDENCIES: A3 (runner core + per-cell loop). Satisfies parent AC3 and AC5.

ACCEPTANCE (numbered; Test* symbols in scripts/benchmark/tests/concurrency.bats):
1. Test_budget_halt_produces_budget_halted: `./scripts/benchmark/benchmark --profile sindri-lucebox --bench-set tb-2-1-canary --max-cost-usd 0.01` produces at least one cell with final_status=budget_halted (parent AC3).
2. Test_sigterm_marks_interrupted: SIGTERM to a mid-sweep run marks in-flight cells final_status=interrupted (process_outcome=killed) (parent AC5).

4. Test_sigterm_exit_nonzero: the interrupted run exits non-zero (parent AC5), verified by `./benchmark ... & sleep 5; kill -TERM $!; wait; jq .final_status bench/results/.../report.json`.
5. Test_concurrency_flock_serializes_group: two cells in the same concurrency-group never hold the group lock simultaneously, and in-flight.json prunes dead-PID entries.

description:
PROBLEM
A dead local provider endpoint costs ~30 seconds of wall-clock per call before Fizeau surfaces the dial error. The fizeau-8134d6db AC required dial-class failures to bail in under 5 seconds; the shipped implementation only short-circuits the *retry loop* (one attempt instead of four), but the *dial itself* still uses Go's default TCP connect timeout (~30s on Linux). Observed today: every bead routed to bragi:1234 / bragi:8020 / grendel:1234 / grendel:1235 / grendel:8000 took ~30s to fail with "dial tcp ... i/o timeout". With 14 beads in the ddx queue all routing to a single dead host, the drain spent ~7 minutes establishing that the host was dead — meeting fizeau-8134d6db's letter (single attempt) while missing its spirit (under 5s).

ROOT CAUSE
internal/core/loop.go:643 (IsDialError short-circuit) is correctly wired. The retry-loop layer fails fast.

What is NOT bounded: the underlying http.Transport's DialContext. internal/provider/openai/openai.go and internal/sdk/openaicompat construct openaicompat.Config without overriding the HTTP client's transport. Go's net/http default Transport has no explicit DialContext, so it uses net.Dialer{} with Timeout=0 — which on Linux waits for the kernel's full TCP SYN retransmit timeout (≈21s + RTO backoff = 30s observed). For a known-local endpoint that the operator just unplugged, 30s is pure waste.

PROPOSED FIX
- Configure an explicit net.Dialer with Timeout=5s (or ServiceOptions-driven, defaulting to 5s) in the openaicompat client construction path.
- Wrap http.Transport.DialContext so the connect phase is bounded independent of the request streaming timeout.
- Keep the request-streaming timeout (Timeout field) separate — large requests legitimately take minutes once connected.
- Expose ConnectTimeout in openaicompat.Config so callers (DDx, benchmarks) can tune for high-latency networks if needed; default 5s.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change the retry-loop short-circuit (already correct).
- Do not change in-flight 5xx retry behavior.
- Do not bound the request body / streaming timeout in this bead.

DEPS
None.
title: routing: bound TCP dial timeout to ~5s, not Go default ~30s

description:
Killing a sweep parent (run_terminalbench_2_1_sweep.sh PID) does not currently kill its descendant matrix-runner / harbor children. They are reparented to init (PPID=1) and keep executing. Concrete failures this session:

1. **2026-05-11 ~22:30Z** — Killed the local-lane sweep (PID 463900). Vidar matrix-runner child kept running on the dead oMLX server, wasted 70 cells with retry-spam pattern before I noticed.

2. **2026-05-11 ~18:15Z** — Killed the timing-baseline ds4 sweep (PID 942197) after the reasoning-not-supported bug. The matrix-runner became orphan (945491, PPID=1). Then I launched a replacement (991522 → 999500) and a second iteration (975660, orphan). All three were running simultaneously against ds4's single graph worker, contending for the slot and writing to the same report.json paths. Smoke tests timed out because of slot contention. Took ~30 min to notice and clean up.

The general pattern: any time we `kill -KILL <sweep_pid>` to restart with new config (multiplier change, profile fix, server-side issue), one or more children survive. They consume identical work, race the new sweep, and corrupt the per-cell results.

PROPOSED FIX

Two interlocking pieces:

A. **run_terminalbench_2_1_sweep.sh: trap signals + propagate.** Add a trap handler in the shell script that on SIGTERM/SIGINT/EXIT:
   - Records the matrix-runner PIDs as they spawn
   - On signal, sends SIGTERM to each matrix-runner PID; if still alive after 10s, SIGKILL
   - Then exits

B. **cmd/bench (sweep + matrix subcommands): handle SIGTERM by killing harbor children.** When fiz-bench receives SIGTERM, propagate to in-flight `harbor run` subprocesses (exec.CommandContext already supports this via context cancellation). The existing `cmd.Cancel = func() error { return cmd.Process.Signal(syscall.SIGTERM) }` is correct shape; verify it actually fires on parent SIGTERM and not just on context.WithTimeout.

C. **Alternative (single-knob fix): process groups.** Have the sweep script start fiz-bench in its own process group (`setpgid`), and have the kill path send SIGTERM to the entire process group (`kill -TERM -<pgid>`). One signal takes out the whole tree atomically. Simpler than A+B; downside is no graceful per-process shutdown order.

In-scope files:
- scripts/benchmark/run_terminalbench_2_1_sweep.sh — trap handler + PID tracking
- cmd/bench/sweep.go and cmd/bench/matrix.go — signal handling on the Go side (verify existing exec.CommandContext + cmd.Cancel work as intended on SIGTERM, not just context cancel)
- Tests / integration: confirm a `kill -TERM $sweep_pid` reaps the entire process tree within 30s.

Out-of-scope:
- Persistent state recovery (sweep resume from interrupted cell). Already handled by --resume + report.json being the durable state.
- Distinguishing "user-initiated kill" from "supervisor-initiated kill" — both should cleanly shut down.

description:
PROBLEM
The current root has an uncommitted but coherent route-health fix: execute dispatch failures emit `routing_actual` in the final event, but the service does not record that failed provider/model attempt into route health. A subsequent `ResolveRoute` can pick the same failed provider again even when the final event already classifies the failure as transport/availability/protocol.

PROPOSED FIX
Record route attempts from final execution events when `RoutingActual` is present. Record successes and dispatchability failures; ignore semantic/non-dispatch failures. Split endpoint-qualified providers with the existing endpoint/provider helper. Add a regression test proving a transport failure from `Execute` causes the next `ResolveRoute` to reject the failed provider as unhealthy.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- service_execute.go
- service_execute_dispatch.go
- service_route_attempts.go
- service_route_attempts_test.go

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change route scoring weights or route selection policy beyond feeding existing route health.
- Do not record semantic/model-output failures as provider health failures.
- Do not modify DDx tracker files by hand.

None.

acceptance: scripts/benchmark/benchmark-evidence.schema.json carries 'runtime_props' (optional object). New package implements at least 4 platform extractors (llamacpp, vllm, ds4, omlx) with tests. Bench runner stamps runtime_props into each cell when the platform supports it; missing/failed extraction is logged but non-fatal. go test ./... passes. docs/benchmarks/ has a runtime-props.md note.
description:
When a bench cell runs, capture the server-reported runtime properties for the (provider, model) it ran against and persist them in the cell evidence. The point: many cell-cell deltas (MTP on/off, speculative decoder configs, kv-quant variants) are NOT in the lane definition — they vary by server config or per-request flags. Capturing server-reported props per cell makes the comparison grid self-describing and lets us run more attempts with parameter sweeps rather than pre-declaring every combination as a separate lane.

Scope:
1. Schema: extend scripts/benchmark/benchmark-evidence.schema.json with a new optional 'runtime_props' object on the evidence record. Fields it should accommodate (all optional): base_model, model_quant, kv_quant, draft_model, draft_mode (e.g. mtp, dflash, eagle), max_context, sampling defaults (temperature, top_p, top_k, repeat_penalty), build_info, server_version, gpu_layers, mtp_enabled, speculative_n, plus a free-form 'platform_raw' blob preserving the original server response for grep-ability.

2. Per-platform extractors in a new package (e.g. internal/benchmark/runtimeprops/ with one file per platform):
   - llamacpp: GET /props (the canonical metadata endpoint)
   - vllm: GET /v1/models + best-effort /metrics or /server_info
   - ds4: investigate the server's exposed metadata endpoint (try /v1/models, /health, /props, /metadata; pick the richest one returning useful fields)
   - omlx: similar — likely just /v1/models for now
   - rapid-mlx: similar
   - lucebox: investigate the dflash server's metadata surface
   - openai/openrouter: just record model_id from response, no extra fetch
3. Integration: the bench runner calls the appropriate extractor once per cell (after preflight, before bench start), stamps runtime_props into the evidence record. Failure to fetch must NOT fail the cell — log a 'runtime_props.extraction_failed: reason' and continue.

4. Tests: per-platform extractor unit tests with canned response fixtures; schema validator confirms runtime_props is accepted.

5. Documentation: brief notes in docs/benchmarks/ on what runtime_props captures, where it lives in the cell, and how to add a new platform extractor.
title: Capture per-cell runtime props from supported platforms

description:
DEFERRED. Filed proposed-status for future work.

OpenRouter routes a single model (e.g. qwen/qwen3.6-27b) to multiple
upstream sub-providers (DeepInfra, Together, Fireworks, etc.). Each
has its own pricing, latency, context window, and rate limits. For
high-fidelity routing, the snapshot should distinguish them.

## Syntax (per ADR-012 naming convention)

`<provider>/<model>@<sub_provider>`. Examples:
- `openrouter/qwen/qwen3.6-27b@deepinfra`
- `openrouter/qwen/qwen3.6-27b@together`
- `openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6@anthropic`

## Source

OR's `/api/v1/models/<id>/endpoints` returns:
```
{
  "data": {
    "endpoints": [
      {"provider_name": "DeepInfra", "context_length": ..., ...},
      {"provider_name": "Together", "context_length": ..., ...}
    ]
  }
}
```

## Why deferred

- Per-OR-model API call (N+1 problem; OR has hundreds of models)
- Cardinality blowup in the snapshot (each model becomes N entries)
- Requires routing-layer changes to actually USE the sub-provider
  selection
- Marginal value for current benchmark-mode use case (we're not
  routing through OR at scale)

## Re-evaluate when

- We ship cost-based routing (ADR-011, bead E2) and quota signals
  start mattering across OR sub-providers
- We benchmark OR-Qwen3 across multiple upstream sub-providers and
  see measurable performance differences
- An operator explicitly requests it

## Depends on

- M2 (snapshot assembler) — extension, not parallel implementation

acceptance:
1. CONTRACT-004 and internal/harnesses/types.go define the internal-only exported type PortableRuntimeFileIdentity{Size int64, ContentSHA256 string}; no root-facade alias is added. PortableRuntimeInterpretedClosureRequest defines InterpreterIdentity PortableRuntimeFileIdentity. An identity is valid only when Size > 0 and ContentSHA256 is exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Zero or malformed identities fail with ErrPortableRuntimeClosureIncomplete before interpreter filesystem inspection.
2. AnalyzePortableRuntimeInterpretedClosure selects the interpreter exclusively from the caller-supplied InterpreterSource; it performs no PATH lookup, command execution, or shebang-based interpreter selection. Normal traversal of that interpreter PT_INTERP loader and declared library roots remains required. It resolves an initially supplied symlink chain to a regular final target, opens that target once, verifies path metadata against descriptor.Stat, parses the same-target owner-executable ELF, and computes size and SHA-256 from that same still-open descriptor. Before success it re-stats both descriptor and resolved path and requires unchanged identity, mode, size, and modification time. The emitted interpreter asset uses that descriptor-derived digest. Expected or actual mismatches expose no paths, sizes, digests, or bytes.

description:
PROBLEM: The A2 bash runner has no host-level serialization for exclusive runtimes; concurrent sweeps race on GPUs/runtimes. No bounded job pool exists. No visibility into running cells from outside the process.

ROOT CAUSE:
  - scripts/benchmark/benchmark (A2): per-cell loop runs cells inline with no flock guard, no job-control pool, no shared state file.
  - No state directory convention exists for the bash runner.

PROPOSED FIX:
  1. State dir: $FIZEAU_BENCH_STATE_DIR (default ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/fizeau-benchmark). Subdir locks/, plus <hostname>/in-flight.json.
  2. Per cell: `flock $FIZEAU_BENCH_STATE_DIR/locks/<concurrency-group>.lock` around cell exec; group resolved from profile/bench-set.
  3. --jobs N flag (default 1): bash job-control pool with `wait -n`; bounded by N.
  4. in-flight.json: under a separate flock, append {cell_id,pid,started_at} at cell start, remove at close. On read, prune dead-PID entries.
  5. Hostname segregation so multi-host shared NFS state-dirs do not collide.

NON-SCOPE (preserved from parent):

description:
PROBLEM
The Fizeau repo has 103 .go files at the repo root, all in `package fizeau` (or `package fizeau_test`). This includes service.go, service_routing.go, service_execute*.go, harness_golden_integration_test.go, contract003_*_test.go, metadata_billing.go, options_*.go, provider_*.go, public_api*.go, role_correlation.go, routing_errors*.go, and ~85 other files spanning the entire service surface.

This violates standard Go project layout:
- Library code lives under `internal/` or `pkg/`, not at the repo root.
- Root is typically reserved for CHANGELOG, README, LICENSE, go.mod, and (optionally) the `main` package binary.
- 103 files in one package is hard to navigate; package-level cohesion is lost.

It also creates spurious friction:
- IDE / `gopls` slows on the big package.
- Adding a new top-level helper requires choosing between "another root .go file" and "carve out a subpackage" with no precedent.
- The default ddx execution worktree clones the entire repo including the root .go pile, multiplying disk during the parallel-drain.

ROOT CAUSE
Historical accident. The Fizeau repo grew from a single-file prototype; new files kept landing at the root because that's where the existing service.go lived. There was never an explicit decision to move to internal/.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Create `internal/service/` (or `internal/fizeau/` — choose based on import-name ergonomics).
2. Move all 103 root .go files into the new directory.
3. Rename their package declarations from `package fizeau` / `package fizeau_test` to `package service` / `package service_test` (or the chosen name).
4. Update all imports across the repo (internal/serviceimpl, cmd/fiz, cmd/fizeau, etc.) to reference the new path.
5. Add a thin `service.go` at the root if a public top-level entry point is still needed (or rely on cmd/).
6. Update CONTRACT-003 cross-references that point at root-level types (they're already documented by their type names; just file paths change).

NON-SCOPE
- Don't change the public API surface in CONTRACT-003. Type names and method signatures stay.
- Don't change the test surface — test names + assertions stay.
- Don't reshape the internal/ tree (internal/harnesses, internal/routing, etc. are fine where they are).
- Don't touch internal/serviceimpl until step 5 of the consuming refactor: that package is currently the only place service code is allowed to import per the harness-interface-refactor plan.

DEPS
- Don't start until the harness-interface refactor (plan-2026-05-14-harness-interface-refactor.md) drain completes. The refactor's per-harness migration touches service*.go consumers; doing both in parallel would create constant merge conflicts. Block on the lint rule landing (BEAD-HARNESS-IF-10 / fizeau-1e5bcee1) since that's the final harness-refactor step.
- Coordinate the auto-merge of any other in-flight beads that touch root-level files.

RISK
- Big-diff bead. Every consumer file changes (imports). Tests have to compile and pass against the new path. Recommend a single sweeping PR with `git mv` to preserve blame.
- Use `go build ./...` + `go test ./... -count=1` as the verification command; if either is red, the rewrite isn't done.

description:
PROBLEM
A Claude-TUI process can close its PTY immediately before the Stop-hook payload becomes visible. Fizeau checks once, emits a generic session-closed failure, and discards the process exit evidence. The Stop hook also writes its payload directly to the observed path, so readers can observe a missing or partial file.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
internal/harnesses/claude-tui/harness.go:509-520 performs a single readStopHookPayloadNonce call when Output closes and immediately fails if it misses. internal/harnesses/claude-tui/harness.go:680-683 uses shell redirection directly to stopPayloadPath rather than write-then-rename publication. internal/harnesses/claude-tui/harness.go:119-128 omits wait/exit status from the injected ptyConn surface, and runTurn ignores Close/Wait errors at lines 260-262. Existing TestRunTurnCompletesOnStopNonceOnly keeps the PTY open until after the payload, so it cannot expose the ordering race.

PROPOSED FIX
Publish the Stop payload atomically with a same-directory temporary file plus rename. When PTY EOF wins, wait for a small bounded grace interval while polling only for the matching nonce, then finalize through the transcript contract. If grace expires, emit exactly one failed Final that retains sanitized bounded exit/status evidence without exposing the prompt or full terminal frame. Extend the injectable PTY test surface only as needed to supply deterministic exit evidence.

description:
PROBLEM
The PR A bash runner at scripts/benchmark/benchmark must execute cells concurrently while honoring per-group serialization and must shut down cleanly on SIGINT/SIGTERM. Today cmd/bench/matrix.go:1 owns scheduling and there is no flock-based group lock, no setsid process-group tracking, and no escalation from SIGTERM to SIGKILL.

ROOT CAUSE
The parent scope at cmd/bench/matrix.go:1 (replaced by scripts/benchmark/benchmark) lacks a background-job pool capped by --jobs, lacks flock locking under ${FIZEAU_BENCH_STATE_DIR:-${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/fizeau-benchmark}/locks/<group>.lock, and lacks setsid-based process-group control needed for deterministic signal escalation.

PROPOSED FIX
In scripts/benchmark/benchmark add a background-job pool capped by --jobs. Acquire flock per concurrency group at ${FIZEAU_BENCH_STATE_DIR:-${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/fizeau-benchmark}/locks/<group>.lock so cells in the same group serialize while unrelated groups run concurrently. Start every cell under setsid and record its process group. On SIGINT/SIGTERM stop scheduling new cells, SIGTERM each in-flight process group, wait 30 seconds, then SIGKILL remaining process groups. Tests must use flock-sensitive workers and long-running cell stubs to verify behavior deterministically without requiring real Docker.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change planning semantics, adapter JSON contracts, or report composition except as required to integrate concurrent execution. Do not finalize the PR C bench-set schema. Do not implement the harbor-runner Docker wrapper or image build assets (covered by sibling A4b). Do not require real Docker in unit tests; mock docker where touched. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it. Governing artifact reference governing:plan-2026-05-15-benchmark-runner-simplification must remain. Parent/dependency ID fizeau-11e9c095 must remain traceable. Verification gates cd cli && go test ./... and lefthook run pre-commit are required.

AC
1. TestBenchmarkJobsLimit: run mode never has more than --jobs cells in flight.
2. TestBenchmarkConcurrencyGroupFlock: cells sharing a concurrency group serialize through the configured flock lock path, while unrelated groups may run concurrently.
3. TestBenchmarkSignalTerminatesProcessGroups: SIGINT/SIGTERM stops scheduling new cells, sends SIGTERM to each in-flight process group, waits, and escalates to SIGKILL after the configured timeout.
4. TestBenchmarkVerificationGatesA4a: cd cli && go test ./... passes.
5. TestBenchmarkLefthookGateA4a: lefthook run pre-commit passes.

description:
PROBLEM
Fizeau's subprocess discovery cache receives a bounded refresh context but discards it before live Codex model discovery. A cancelled DDx request or stopped service can therefore return while `codex --no-alt-screen` continues in a PTY refresh, writing caller-owned cache/home state and consuming CPU after the lifecycle that requested it has ended. DDx Niflheim attempts observed these late provider descendants and temp-root teardown races while using Fizeau v0.14.50.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- internal/serviceimpl/subprocess_discovery_cache.go:74-94 defines a discoverycache.Refresher that accepts context.Context but ignores it and calls context-free ModelDiscoveryHarness.DefaultModelSnapshot().
- internal/serviceimpl/subprocess_discovery_cache.go:125-149 schedules warm and cold refresh work; discoverycache supplies the refresh deadline/cancellation context, but the ignored parameter severs that lifecycle before the harness call.
- internal/harnesses/codex/model_discovery.go:20-48 calls ptyquota.Run(context.Background(), ...), so cancellation cannot reach the PTY session even when an upstream caller has a bounded context.
- internal/harnesses/codex/contract004.go:212-224 exposes only the context-free snapshot method and therefore cannot carry refresh cancellation into ReadCodexModelDiscoveryViaPTY.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a backward-compatible context-aware model-discovery surface (for example an optional ContextModelDiscoveryHarness interface) and make subprocessDiscoveryRefresher prefer it with the exact refresh context it receives. Implement the surface for the Codex harness: thread context through DefaultModelSnapshot and ReadCodexModelDiscoveryViaPTY into ptyquota.Run. Keep the existing context-free ModelDiscoveryHarness method as a compatibility wrapper, but do not use that wrapper from the cache when the contextual surface exists. On cancellation, wait for ptyquota/session cleanup so no probe descendant or late cache write survives the refresh.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- internal/harnesses/types.go for the optional context-aware contract
- internal/serviceimpl/subprocess_discovery_cache.go and focused tests
- internal/harnesses/codex/contract004.go
- internal/harnesses/codex/model_discovery.go and focused Unix process-reap tests

NON-SCOPE
Do not remove live model discovery, replace it with static catalog data, extend refresh deadlines, change routing scores, or change stale-while-revalidate semantics. Do not couple background refresh to an already-cancelled request context: use the context supplied by discoverycache, whose owner is the refresh/service lifecycle. Other harness implementations may be migrated in follow-up beads; this bead must establish the generic optional contract and fix the observed Codex path.

PARENT AND DEPS
Root upstream reliability incident for DDx bead ddx-a751a7b1. No dependencies.
title: harness: propagate refresh cancellation into Codex PTY model discovery

description:
Build a CLI at cmd/fizeau-probe-reasoning that snapshots provider
introspection AND verifies whether the upstream actually behaves the way
introspection claims. Per ADR-010 Amendment 2026-05-11, the probe is now
primarily a verification tool, not a discovery tool — introspection
adapters (fizeau-e80c156e) handle discovery where it's available.

Three modes of output per (provider, model):

1. **Snapshot** — verbatim capture of every introspection endpoint the
   provider exposes:
     ds4:           /props, /v1/models, /v1/models/<id>
     llama-server:  /props, /v1/models, /slots, /health, /metrics
     OR:            /api/v1/models, /api/v1/models/<id> if supported
     others:        whatever GET <base>/v1/models returns
   Written verbatim into the artifact directory as JSON files. This is
   the auditable record of \"what the server claimed on date X.\"

2. **Verification matrix** — send a small set of seeded chat completions
   that exercise each documented wire knob:
     - reasoning: off
     - reasoning: low (KindNamed, PortableBudgets=2048)
     - reasoning: medium (KindNamed, PortableBudgets=8192)
     - reasoning: high (KindNamed, PortableBudgets=32768)
     - reasoning: 4096 (KindTokens explicit)
     - reasoning: 16384 (KindTokens explicit)
   For each row capture: wire body sent, finish_reason,
   usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens (if present), len of
   message.reasoning_content, wall time. Hash of <think> block content
   when present (so flat-mapping is visible).

   Use a stable single-prompt with seed pinning when the upstream supports
   it (sampling.seed). Prompt: \"What is 17 times 24? Show your work step
   by step.\" Small enough to run fast (~30-60s per request on local
   lanes); large enough to produce measurable thinking.

3. **Verdict** — one of:
     introspection-trusted: claims and observations match (e.g. ds4's
       alias map predicts low/medium/xhigh produce identical thinking
       depth, and the matrix confirms within sampling noise).
     introspection-divergent: claims and observations disagree. Print
       the disagreement and flag for operator review.
     introspection-absent: no useful introspection endpoint; catalog L2
       required. Print recommended `reasoning_wire` value.

CLI surface:
  fizeau-probe-reasoning --profile <path> [--artifact-dir <path>]
                          [--json] [--snapshot-only]
                          [--matrix-only] [--seed <int>]
  fizeau-probe-reasoning --provider <type> --base-url <url> --model <id>
                          [--api-key-env <var>] ...

Default artifact-dir: /tmp/fizeau-probe-<timestamp>/<provider>/

Run timeout per request: 5 minutes (long-thinking Qwen3 / DS4 can take
60s+ on local hardware).

Makefile: add `make probe-reasoning PROFILE=<path>` target.

In-scope files:
- cmd/fizeau-probe-reasoning/main.go (new)
- cmd/fizeau-probe-reasoning/snapshot.go (new) — introspection endpoint
  capture per provider type.
- cmd/fizeau-probe-reasoning/matrix.go (new) — verification matrix
  runner.
- cmd/fizeau-probe-reasoning/verdict.go (new) — claim-vs-observation
  diff logic.
- cmd/fizeau-probe-reasoning/probe_test.go (new) — table tests against
  recorded fixtures (no live endpoint needed for unit tests).
- Makefile — `probe-reasoning` target.

Out-of-scope:
- Auto-writing back to the catalog (operator reviews and writes
  manually).
- Sweeping multiple models in one invocation (shell loop is fine).
- Real tokenizer for reasoning_content length conversion (use chars/4
  approximation, matching the telemetry bead fizeau-8f62bcbb).

Depends on: fizeau-e80c156e (introspection adapters — probe uses the
same snapshot logic so the two share code).

description:
PROBLEM
A timed-out or cancelled TerminalBench Harbor run can leave Fizeau harness subprocesses alive after Harbor reports the cell as failed. In the local incident on 2026-05-16, the OrbStack VM had 610 gemini-matching processes and the process/swap aggregate showed `gemini` holding about 69,659 MiB total (22,929 MiB RSS + 46,730 MiB swap). System memory was 60/62 GiB used, swap was effectively full, and `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.events` showed `oom_kill 132`. Cleaning up the Gemini/Node processes immediately raised available RAM from about 2 GiB to about 28-36 GiB.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `scripts/benchmark/harbor_agent.py:347-356` builds a bash `cmd=(/installed-agent/fiz ...)` array and runs it as `"${cmd[@]}" 2>&1 | stdbuf -oL tee /logs/agent/fiz.txt`, then reads `PIPESTATUS[0]`. There is no `trap` for TERM/INT/EXIT and no child-process-tree cleanup. If Harbor cancels the Docker exec shell on AgentTimeout, the shell can die while `fiz` or its wrapped subprocess harness (`gemini`, `claude`, `codex`, etc.) remains orphaned.
- `agentcli/run.go:339-341` creates the execution context with `signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt)` only. A SIGTERM from Harbor/runner cancellation is not converted into service context cancellation, so subprocess harness cleanup such as `internal/harnesses/gemini/runner.go:274-287` may not run before the `fiz` process exits.
- `cmd/bench/matrix.go:1097-1104` sends SIGTERM to the Harbor process and gives it 60s `WaitDelay`, but that only assumes Harbor and Docker Compose finalizers clean up the trial. It does not verify or enforce cleanup of the nested `fiz -> harness CLI` process tree that the FizeauAgent shell wrapper starts inside the task container.

PROPOSED FIX
Make cancellation cleanup explicit at both levels:
1. Teach the `fiz` CLI to treat SIGTERM like os.Interrupt for run cancellation on Unix, so the service context is cancelled and harness runners can kill their subprocess groups before the process exits.
2. Rewrite the FizeauAgent generated bash in `scripts/benchmark/harbor_agent.py` so it wraps the `fiz` invocation with TERM/INT/EXIT cleanup. Preserve tee logging and the `fiz_rc` status, but keep the child PID, terminate the child process tree on cancellation, wait a short grace interval, then SIGKILL leftovers. Avoid a bare foreground pipeline where killing the shell loses the child PID.
3. Add or update benchmark-runner cancellation tests so parent cancellation exercises the cleanup path and the generated command structure cannot regress to an untrapped pipeline.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- `agentcli/run.go`
- `agentcli/cli_process_test.go`
- `scripts/benchmark/harbor_agent.py`
- `scripts/benchmark/test_harbor_agent.py`
- `cmd/bench/matrix.go` and `cmd/bench/matrix_test.go` only if runner-level process-group cancellation must change to make the cleanup complete.

NON-SCOPE
- Rewriting the benchmark runner beyond cancellation/cleanup behavior.
- Changing TerminalBench task Docker images.
- Changing Gemini/Codex/Claude harness routing or model selection.
- Bulk deleting existing leaked processes; this bead is for preventing recurrence.

NOTES FOR IMPLEMENTER
The existing `TestCLI_CancelSignal_WritesSessionEndEvent` covers os.Interrupt. Add a SIGTERM equivalent rather than replacing that test. The Python command-builder tests already mock `exec_as_agent`, so they are the right place to assert the generated bash contains the trap/cleanup structure without needing a live Harbor run.

acceptance:
1. TestScorePolicy_MinPowerDoesNotDisableDefaultPolicy asserts that with MinPower=8, the default policy still gives the +15 subscription/free bonus to a free subscription candidate, and that bonus is reflected in candidate.ScoreComponents['quota_health'].
2. TestScorePolicy_MinPowerSonnetBeatsOpus_DefaultPolicy: given two candidates (sonnet power=8 cost=0 subscription quota_ok; opus power=10 cost=0.045 subscription quota_ok), with MinPower=8, the sonnet candidate's total score is higher than opus.
3. TestScorePolicy_MaxPowerDoesNotDisableProviderPreference asserts that with MaxPower=8 set, a 'subscription-first' provider preference still adds the +30 quota_health bonus.
4. Existing service_routing_test.go tests (TestRouteWith* etc.) still pass — regression guard for non-power-bounded scoring.
5. go test ./internal/routing/... ./... -count=1 passes.
description:
PROBLEM
internal/routing/score.go:60 and :108 wrap the policy-aware scoring (cheap/default/smart preferences for local/subscription/cost) and the provider-preference bias in `if !hasPowerBounds`. When a caller sets --min-power N or --max-power M, those branches are skipped entirely. Result: among candidates that all satisfy the bounds, the routing falls through to raw base+quota+power-9-bonus scoring, which systematically prefers higher-power-metered models over equivalent-quality subscription-free models.

Observed today: ddx try --harness claude --min-power 8 routed to claude/opus (power 10, score ~76, metered ~$0.045/turn) instead of claude/claude-sonnet-4-6 (power 8, score 186 per fiz route-status without bounds, subscription/free). Across the 11 harness-interface refactor bead executions, this cost real opus tokens for work sonnet would have handled fine.

ROOT CAUSE
- score.go:52: hasPowerBounds := cand.MinPower > 0 || cand.MaxPower > 0
- score.go:60: `if !hasPowerBounds { switch policy ... }` — the entire policy preference block (deployment locality, quota health, cost-class ranking) is gated off
- score.go:108: `if !hasPowerBounds { switch cand.ProviderPreference ... }` — provider-preference bias gated off

The intent was probably: 'when user expresses explicit power bounds, just enforce bounds and ignore default biases.' But power bounds are orthogonal to policy preference — a user asking for power>=8 still wants the cheaper, subscription-backed candidate among the eligible set.

PROPOSED FIX
Remove the `if !hasPowerBounds` guards at score.go:60 and score.go:108. Apply policy preference and provider-preference bias unconditionally to in-bounds candidates. Keep the below-MinPower / above-MaxPower penalties as they are (lines 227-238) — those correctly demote out-of-bounds candidates without disabling policy scoring for in-bounds ones.

The natural-power bonus at line 222 (`Power * 12` when no bounds set) can stay gated — that's a different signal: 'when no bounds expressed, treat higher power as a quality proxy.' When bounds ARE expressed, the bounds themselves encode the power preference; double-counting via natural-power-bonus would be wrong.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change the below-MinPower / above-MaxPower penalty values (lines 227-238).
- Do not change the natural-power bonus gating at line 222.
- Do not change quota-pressure, cooldown, sticky-affinity, or perf scoring.
- Do not introduce new score components.
title: routing: policy-aware scoring is skipped when MinPower/MaxPower set, preferring expensive opus over free sonnet

description:
Implement or tighten Fizeau's synchronous refresh coordinator so stale health/quota/model facts are refreshed through one lock-coordinated path instead of each CLI process launching its own probes.

Desired behavior:
- Fizeau has no required daemon; its contract is synchronous refresh plus cross-process locks, single-flight/coalescing, TTLs, cooldowns, bounded concurrency, and atomic snapshot writes.
- Repeated refresh requests for the same provider/field class coalesce into one in-flight operation per TTL/cooldown window.
- Refreshes are bounded, concurrent, and per-provider rate/cooldown aware.
- Routing-relevant refresh covers health, quota, model availability/discovery, context/tools/reasoning support, billing/effective cost metadata where dynamic, and utilization if available.
- Refresh results update the fiz models snapshot atomically with version/timestamp/freshness metadata.
- Refresh failure records refresh_failed/stale state for scoring and diagnostics; it must not create an unbounded retry loop.
- Long-running callers such as a DDx server can maintain async freshness by invoking this synchronous API from their own heartbeat; route correctness must not depend on that integration.

In scope: cache/refresh coordinator internals, process lock/single-flight logic, public refresh/warmup entrypoint for long-running callers, focused tests using fake refreshers.

Out of scope: CLI flag UX; route scoring; changing DDx upstream server behavior if that lives outside this repo.
title: Add refresh coordinator semantics without CLI refresh storms

description:
EPIC for the available-models snapshot architecture. The user-facing
deliverable is a `fiz models` CLI subcommand. The architectural
deliverable is the foundation for the auto-router: a runtime-resolved
view of "what can fizeau actually use right now," assembled from all
discovery sources, enriched with catalog metadata, surfaced through a
multi-process-safe disk cache.

## End goal

For a given fizeau install at a given time, there is a canonical set
of known models — one entry per (provider, model_id) — with defined
properties: identity, parsed family/version/tier, catalog-derived
power/cost/reasoning_levels/quota_pool, and runtime-derived status/
quota_remaining/recent latency. Operators introspect via `fiz models`;
routing reads the same snapshot to score candidates. Single source of
truth; no separate "what does routing think exists" vs "what does
operator see" divergence.

## Child beads (in dependency order)

- **M0** (ADR-012): per-source on-disk cache for discovery + runtime
  signals. Defines file layout, locking semantics, single-flight
  refresh algorithm, atomic-write contract, test matrix.
- **M1**: cache infrastructure — implements ADR-012's algorithm with
  the 10-test robustness matrix. Includes `ParseModelRef`/canonical
  identity helpers.
- **M2**: snapshot assembler — enumerate providers (incl harnesses-
  as-providers) → discover via cache → parse via tier-ranker
  (depends on routing bead A) → enrich from catalog (joins on
  power, cost, reasoning_levels, quota_pool from bead E1).
- **M3**: runtime signal collector — status, quota_remaining, recent
  p50 latency → runtime cache.
- **M4**: `fiz models` top-level CLI subcommand. Default filtered
  view; `--include-noise --refresh --no-refresh --json --provider X
  --power-min/max`. Detail view via `fiz models <ref>` with shortform
  fuzzy resolution and full-canonical exact match.
- **M5** (deferred): OR sub-provider expansion via `@<sub_provider>`
  syntax. Filed proposed-status; future work.

## Architecture invariants

1. **Identity = (provider, model_id).** Canonical form `<provider>/
   <model_id>`. Provider names slug-safe; model IDs preserved
   provider-side. Split-on-first-slash.
2. **Harness == provider** for snapshot purposes. Subscription harness
   wrappers participate as named providers (e.g.,
   `claude-subscription`, `codex-subscription`).
3. **Catalog is implementation detail.** No catalog-only entries
   appear in `fiz models`. If no provider serves a model, it's not
   "known."
4. **No aliases in snapshot.** Aliases are a search/discovery
   concern (CLI-side fuzzy resolution); snapshot stores canonical
   entries only.
5. **Per-source on-disk cache**, multi-process-safe, with strict
   100ms UI budget. Discovery cache long-TTL; runtime cache short-TTL.
6. **Single-flight refresh** across processes via PID+marker pattern
   (extending fizeau's existing `acquireMatrixLock` idiom).
7. **Stale-while-revalidate** by default. Force-refresh waits.
8. **Atomic write** via tmp+fsync+rename. No torn reads.

## Governing doc updates

- **NEW: ADR-012** — per-source disk cache for discovery + runtime
- **FEAT-006** (standalone CLI) — add `fiz models` subcommand
- **FEAT-004** (model routing) — addendum: routing reads snapshot
- **ADR-009** (routing surface redesign) — addendum: harness-as-
  provider in snapshot

## Closes when

All five active children (M0, M1, M2, M3, M4) closed. M5 is filed
proposed-status as future work and does not block this epic.

description:
PROBLEM: Concurrent sweeps must not stampede a shared model server; Ctrl-C/SIGTERM must leave clean, attributable state and stop containers; runs must honor a USD cap and halt before overspending.

ROOT CAUSE: concurrency, signal cleanup, and cost accounting are Go-internal in cmd/bench/matrix.go (e.g., the per-cell context timeout at cmd/bench/matrix.go:1107) with no shell equivalent; the bash runner must reimplement them on top of the A3 execution loop.

PROPOSED FIX (scripts/benchmark/benchmark run mode):
- Concurrency: flock per concurrency-group at ${FIZEAU_BENCH_STATE_DIR:-${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/fizeau-benchmark}/locks/<group>.lock; setsid for each cell process group; background-job pool capped by --jobs. Concurrent-cells state at ${FIZEAU_BENCH_STATE_DIR}/<hostname>/in-flight.json: append the cell under flock at start, read current count, write count into the cell, remove at close, prune stale (dead-PID) entries on next read.

description:
Currently when fiz makes an llm.request and gets no llm.response back (cloud-side hang, 5xx, stream-aborted, rate-limit drop, etc.), the cell ends up as a normal graded_fail with reward=0, turns=0, terminated_mid_work=None. The matrix runner treats it identically to a real model failure — even though no actual model attempt happened. Result: 54 of OR-Qwen's 239 "failures" (22%) on TB-2.1 are this class, polluting the pass-rate denominator and wasting the cell entirely.

Two complementary fixes:

A. **Matrix-side classifier rule** (low-effort, high-impact):
   In cmd/bench/matrix_invalid.go, add: if final_status="graded_fail" AND
   (turns is nil OR turns==0) AND terminated_mid_work is nil AND (input_tokens
   is nil OR input_tokens==0), classify as `invalid_provider`. The existing
   `--retry-invalid` flag will then re-run these on the next sweep pass.
   Mirrors the same structural-rule pattern as the recent harness_crash →
   invalid_setup and ran-no-attempt → invalid_setup additions.

B. **In-fiz request-level retry** (deeper, may belong in a separate bead):
   When fiz issues an llm.request and gets no streamed tokens within
   provider_timeout, retry with exponential backoff (e.g. 1s, 4s, 16s)
   up to 3 attempts before failing the turn. Should be capped by total
   wall budget. This stops the request from ever reaching "no llm.response"
   state in the first place. Requires care to avoid amplifying real
   server-side stalls into runaway retries.

1. With a stub provider that returns HTTP 200 with empty body (simulating
   the no-response state), `go test ./cmd/bench/... -run TestClassifyMatrixInvalid`

3. (Optional, defer to Part B bead) `internal/core/loop_test.go` covers
   the retry-on-empty-response behavior with a stub provider that yields
   nothing on the first 2 attempts and a normal response on the 3rd.

In-scope files for Part A (this bead):

- cmd/bench/testdata/matrix-invalid/no-llm-response.json — new fixture

description: PROBLEM: The full race gate intermittently fails TestCatalogCache_StaleServesCachedAndAsyncRefreshes because the test treats a callback-start channel as proof that CatalogCache.probe has committed FetchedAt. ROOT CAUSE: The callback signals before returning; the cache acquires its mutex and writes the refreshed entry only afterward, so the next Get can legitimately observe the old timestamp. A same-key public Get is not a deterministic completion barrier either: it can classify the old entry, then miss a just-completed singleflight and start a legitimate third probe. PROPOSED FIX: Use a two-phase blocked refresh callback, register a test-only DoChan waiter on the known-active same-key singleflight before releasing the callback, await the committed result, then verify the next public Get is a fresh cache hit. Preserve the exact refreshed-timestamp and exactly-two-probe contracts. NON-SCOPE: Do not change production cache ordering, API, TTLs, singleflight behavior, or use sleeps/eventual polling/production hooks.
notes: Implemented in 85233b24 and independently approved. The test now joins the known-active same-key singleflight before release, verifies exact publication and fresh public Get behavior, and passed focused race count=100 plus the repository-wide race pre-push gate.

description:
PROBLEM
Fizeau routes to local LMStudio/MLX endpoints that are demonstrably dead at dispatch time, burning 5-second i/o timeouts per dispatch and pinning sticky leases to dead hosts. Symptom from this morning: bragi-club-3090 / vidar / grendel all timed out on direct TCP probes at the time of investigation, yet Fizeau routed to bragi-club-3090 with `source_status: "available"` and `eligible: true` in the routing_decision event.

ROOT CAUSE
The catalog cache (service_catalog_cache.go) treats GET /v1/models probe failures as the SOLE signal source for the UnreachableAt timestamp. Chat-completions dispatch failures (POST /v1/chat/completions returning `dial tcp ...: i/o timeout`, `connection refused`, etc.) are NOT fed back into the cache. The next routing pass within FreshTTL (60s) re-reads the same stale "available" entry and re-selects the dead endpoint.

Concrete code path:
- service_catalog_cache.go:80 — `UnreachableAt time.Time // zero unless last attempt produced a ReachabilityError`
- service_catalog_cache.go:295-307 — the ONLY writes to UnreachableAt are inside `probe()`, set when probeFn returns `*openai.ReachabilityError`.
- service_probe.go:164-184 — probeOpenAIModels is the probeFn; it classifies GET /v1/models failures into ReachabilityError. Chat-completions failures never reach this function.
- Dispatch code in service_execute.go / the harness HTTP path returns transport errors directly to the caller. No code path calls `cache.MarkUnreachable(endpoint)` (no such API exists) or otherwise touches `e.UnreachableAt` from the dispatch flow.

Compound the cache behavior with two further amplifiers:
1. **Per-CLI-invocation cache isolation.** Each `ddx work` (and each `ddx run`) spawns its own fizeau service in-process; the catalog cache is local heap. ddx-on-project-A's worker may know bragi is unreachable; ddx-on-project-B's worker has an empty cache and probes bragi successfully once (at startup), then trusts that result for FreshTTL (60s) + StaleTTL (10min stale-while-revalidate).
2. **Stale-while-revalidate widens the false-positive window.** service_catalog_cache.go:240 returns the stale-but-cached "available" entry and kicks an async refresh. Synchronous callers receive `available` without waiting for the refresh result.

EVIDENCE FROM DOWNSTREAM DDX
Routing decision for the failed dispatch (.ddx/executions/20260516T174611-788fbe14/embedded/svc-*.jsonl):

  candidate: bragi-club-3090
  source_status: "available"
  eligible: true
  score: 35
  model_discovery_freshness_at: 2026-05-16T17:46:14.952Z

Session.end event 7 seconds later:

  status: error
  error: "agent: provider error: openai: Post \"http://bragi:8020/v1/chat/completions\": dial tcp 100.127.38.115:8020: i/o timeout"
  duration_ms: 5027

Direct TCP test from the same host at the time of investigation: `timeout 5 bash -c 'echo > /dev/tcp/bragi/8020'` failed. Same result on grendel:* and vidar:* (all dead). Yet fizeau's auto-route enumerated bragi/grendel/vidar as `source_status: "available"` because the catalog cache had not been told they were unreachable — only chat-completions had observed the timeout, and the chat-completions path does not write back to the cache.

A separate ddx routing-decision from 24 minutes earlier (different project, same hosts, different fizeau service instance) DID correctly mark bragi-club-3090 as `eligible: false, filter_reason: "endpoint_unreachable"` — but that instance had freshly probed and the probe had failed. The per-instance cache isolation means the "dead" knowledge does not propagate to other service instances.

PROPOSED FIX

1. **Add a dispatch-feedback hook on the catalog cache.** Add a method `cache.RecordDispatchError(endpoint, err error)` (or similar). The dispatch code path in service_execute.go (and any other place where chat-completions is invoked through an OpenAI-compatible adapter) calls this after a failed request. RecordDispatchError classifies err via the same `isNetworkFailure` / `isServerError` predicates that service_probe.go:188-223 already uses; if classified as ReachabilityError-equivalent, set `e.UnreachableAt = time.Now()` and `e.LastErr = err`. Honor the same UnreachableCooldown semantics so the next route pass excludes the endpoint.

2. **Tighten FreshTTL for local subprocess endpoints.** 60s is reasonable for stable cloud APIs but too lenient for laptop-class local servers that suspend/resume (LMStudio on a sleeping MacBook). Either make FreshTTL configurable per provider class, or default it to 10s for `deployment_class: local` and keep 60s for managed_cloud_*.

3. **Make UnreachableCooldown start counting from MOST RECENT failure, not first.** Today UnreachableAt is set once on probe failure and cleared on next success. If dispatch failures repeatedly recur but no probe runs in between, UnreachableAt may be stale. (3) is dependent on (1); without (1), only probes write UnreachableAt so this is moot.

4. **(Optional, larger)** Persist UnreachableAt across service instances via a small on-disk cache file (`~/.cache/fizeau/route-health.json` or similar) with TTL. So `ddx work` invocations across projects share aliveness knowledge, eliminating the per-process false-positive window. NON-SCOPE for this bead; track as follow-up if (1)+(2) prove insufficient.

NON-SCOPE
- Sticky lease vs aliveness interaction (separate bead worth filing; today's evidence is that sticky DID NOT override aliveness in this case — the bug is upstream of sticky in the cache).
- DDX-side changes; ddx passes policy=default verbatim per CONTRACT-003. Fix is entirely Fizeau-side.
- Building the persistent cross-process cache (option 4 above).

CROSS-REF
- fizeau-80d4bf41 (auto-route candidate enumeration collapses multi-tier subscription harnesses to DefaultModel only) — same symptom surface, different root cause.
- fizeau-0bc93861 (openrouter: drop from candidate pool when credential or credit is missing) — same pattern (provider health gating), different provider class.
- Github issue mirror: file as a follow-up to https://github.com/easel/fizeau/issues/6 once this is filed.

description:
A dead local OpenAI-compatible provider (example: grendel rapid-mlx at http://grendel:8000/v1) can still delay or poison unpinned route selection before the routing engine chooses a healthy subscription harness. The current shared service path calls buildRoutingInputsWithCatalog(..., RefreshIfStale), which synchronously calls refreshLocalHealthForRouting and synchronous model snapshot refresh before scoring. This affects ResolveRoute directly, Execute via resolveExecuteRouteWithEngine, route-status, and override telemetry's stripped ResolveRoute call.

Required contract: local/fixed provider liveness and model discovery must be cached signals on the route hot path. Stale or missing local-provider facts may request a coordinated asynchronous refresh, but they must not block unpinned autorouting or explicit non-local harness selection. Provider contact failures must be recorded as route evidence/cooldown when observed, but failure to contact a local provider must not prevent selection of another eligible harness/provider. If every candidate is unavailable, routing must still fail with a typed no-viable-provider style error rather than hanging or aborting the process.

acceptance:
1. CONTRACT-004 defines StateProjections as a closed value-opaque mapping from exact config plus credential/quota/cache asset targets into an activation-owned home/config/data/cache/state directory. File mode bits alone are explicitly insufficient: activation must prevent write, unlink, rename, replacement, and shadowing of config members while permitting declared writable state and generated siblings.
2. Internal types expose PortableRuntimeStateProjectionEntry{AssetTarget,Target}, PortableRuntimeStateProjection{Directory,Entries}, and PortableRuntimeContribution.StateProjections. NormalizePortableRuntimeContribution deep-copies and deterministically sorts both levels and returns typed redacted ErrPortableRuntimeClosureIncomplete failures.
3. TestPortableRuntimeMixedStateProjection proves valid config-plus-state composition, deterministic projection/entry ordering, and bidirectional deep ownership.
4. Rejection cases cover empty/runtime/tmp directories, absolute/traversal/backslash/empty entry targets, missing asset references, unsupported/executable asset kinds, no config member, no credential/quota/cache seed, duplicate or ancestor/descendant outputs/directories, required-absent overlap, reused asset references, and diagnostics containing a source path or fixture secret. Source symlink/escape rejection remains in contributor and materializer tests, not the metadata-only normalizer.
5. CONTRACT-003, CONTRACT-004, ADR-014, implementation plan, and release checklist distinguish unprojected prefix-preserving seeds from projection-consumed seeds. fizeau-b1eefdf6 persists normalized projections and revalidates source identity/symlinks; fizeau-f5bc15e9 generically assembles them and names tests proving config write/unlink/rename/replacement denial while credential refresh, lock creation, and sibling state creation succeed.
6. go test ./internal/harnesses -run 'TestPortableRuntimeMixedStateProjection|TestPortableRuntime.*Projection' -count=1, go test ./... -count=1, git diff --check, ddx doc stale, ddx doc validate, ddx doc audit, and lefthook run pre-commit pass.
description:
PROBLEM: Gemini and Pi keep immutable configuration and mutable credentials in the same native harness-owned directory, while the portable contract currently separates read-only config assets from writable data/state/cache seeds and forbids overlapping targets. A contributor cannot truthfully preserve native paths or credential refresh without a typed projection. Read-only file modes alone are insufficient because a harness UID with a writable parent can unlink, rename, replace, or shadow the config member.

PROPOSED FIX: Add PortableRuntimeStateProjectionEntry{AssetTarget,Target}, PortableRuntimeStateProjection{Directory,Entries}, and Contribution.StateProjections. The generic value-opaque mapping assembles exact declared immutable config members plus credential/quota/cache seeds in one activation-owned native directory. Normalization remains filesystem-independent; contributor discovery and materialization own source identity/symlink checks. Activation must expose config entries through an enforcement boundary that denies write, unlink, rename, replacement, and shadowing while allowing writable state refresh, lock files, and generated siblings.

NON-SCOPE: No Gemini/Pi package discovery, Node analysis, filesystem copying, public facade, OCI orchestration, process start, or harness-specific branching.
notes: Read-only adversarial review on 2026-07-16 corrected three readiness defects before implementation: normalization is metadata-only and must not Lstat projected sources; the previous unseeded-writable-target phrase had no schema meaning; and chmod cannot protect a config file inside a writable directory from unlink/rename/replacement. The reviewed smallest schema uses exact asset references and activation-owned guest destinations, with asset Kind as the sole mutability authority. Contributor/materializer layers retain source symlink and TOCTOU checks.
title: runtime: represent mixed native state projections

PROBLEM
Final release-candidate CI passed gosec, website-smoke, and rename-noise, then failed in `make test-no-race`. One reproducible local failure is `internal/modelregistry/TestAssembleFixtureIncludesDiscoveredProviderModels`: `TempDir RemoveAll cleanup: unlinkat .../discovery: directory not empty`.

ROOT CAUSE
The fixture-oriented modelregistry assemble tests call `Assemble`, whose default is `RefreshBackground`. For providers that also have props/endpoint discovery sources without test fixtures, Assemble can start background refresh work under the test temp cache. The test can finish while that goroutine is still writing/removing marker files, racing `t.TempDir` cleanup.

PROPOSED FIX
Use `AssembleWithOptions(... RefreshNone)` in fixture-only assemble tests that are asserting preloaded cache data, preserving explicit background-refresh coverage in the dedicated refresh coordinator tests.

description:
PROBLEM
Fizeau has no proactive aliveness check for configured providers. A dead local provider (e.g. bragi:1234, grendel:1234) is only learned to be dead by attempting a request against it and eating the dial timeout. The failure feedback is stored in internal/routehealth.Store, which is:
1. Process-local (sync.RWMutex map; not persisted to disk).
2. Short-TTL (DefaultCooldown = 30s; entries expire and are re-tried).

Result for an operator with bragi unplugged but configured:
- Every fresh `ddx work` or `ddx try` process re-probes bragi on its first routing decision, eating a 5s dial timeout (post fizeau-b5757624) or 30s pre-fix.
- Even within a long-running `ddx work --watch`, the route exclusion expires every 30s and bragi gets re-attempted on the next cycle.
- Aggregate cost over a 27-bead drain on 2026-05-14: minutes of dial timeouts and routing thrash, leaking into operator-visible queue stalls.

A quota-recovery probe loop exists at service_probe.go for providers marked `quota_exhausted` (periodic, with retry-after backoff). It does NOT cover `provider_connectivity` failures — those have no proactive recovery path.

ROOT CAUSE
- internal/routehealth/store.go owns failure tracking; it is in-memory only, with no persistence interface (verified by file listing: only store.go / lease_store.go / utilization_store.go — no persist.go).
- service_probe.go's QuotaRecoveryProber only handles ProviderQuotaStateStore — not RouteHealth failures.
- No service-startup probe for configured providers. Providers in fizeau config are trusted to be reachable until a request proves otherwise.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Add a startup aliveness probe to internal/provider/openai/reachability.go (or a new internal/routehealth/probe.go). For each configured provider with a non-cloud base_url, run a single TCP-connect probe (bounded ~2s) on Service.New(). Record the result in routehealth.Store via a new RecordProbe(key, success, observedAt) method.
2. Add a periodic background probe loop (mirroring runQuotaRecoveryProbeLoop in service_probe.go): re-probe providers whose last probe is older than HealthProbeInterval (default 60s). Bound to local-ish providers — skip the cloud subscription routes that handle their own health.
3. Make routehealth.Store optionally persistent. ServiceOptions.PersistRouteHealth path (already proposed in fizeau-7cd66e6b) writes the probe + failure cache to a JSON snapshot with HealthSignalTTL (default 10 min). Subsequent processes read the snapshot at startup so a fresh ddx try doesn't re-discover bragi-is-dead.
4. Extend the routing gate: a candidate whose endpoint has a Probe.Success=false within HealthSignalTTL is FILTERED (not just score-demoted) when alternates exist. New FilterReason: endpoint_unreachable.
5. RouteDecision evidence: include the probe state (last_probe_at, last_probe_success) for each candidate so operators can audit why a candidate was filtered.

NON-SCOPE
- Don't probe cloud subscription routes (claude, openrouter, etc.) — those have their own health story via quota probing.
- Don't change the connection-failure retry policy (fizeau-8134d6db already shipped: 1 attempt, fail fast).
- Don't introduce a daemon — the periodic probe runs inside Service goroutines, same lifetime as quota-recovery loop.
- Don't probe at request time — request-time dial is the existing reactive path; this bead adds proactive probing on a separate schedule.

DEPS
- Composes with fizeau-7cd66e6b (persist route-health across processes) — same persistence layer.
- Composes with fizeau-361f4f4b (router reliability epic) — provides the missing aliveness signal that epic's AC #1 ("fall through to subscription within one decision") depends on.
title: routing: proactive endpoint aliveness probing and durable cache for local providers

a bash runner; ports the matrix-side Python harness_adapters/ to shell harness-adapters/;
wraps Harbor invocation in a Docker container so the host stops needing Python.

CONTEXT: today's runner is `fiz-bench matrix` (Go, cmd/bench/matrix.go ~2232 LOC). It
puts repo root on host PYTHONPATH (cmd/bench/matrix.go:1105) so Harbor can import
scripts.benchmark.harbor_adapters.*. That makes host Python required. We're moving
Harbor and its plugins into a fizeau-harbor-runner Docker image so the host only needs
bash + Node + Docker. The new runner is at scripts/benchmark/benchmark (no extension).

SCOPE — runner (scripts/benchmark/benchmark, new bash script):
  - Arg parsing + dispatch: ./benchmark <subcommand> ... with subcommands
      profiles | bench-sets | task-executors | harness-adapters | validate |
      preflight | (no subcommand = run mode)
  - Run mode flags: --profile P[,P2,...] --bench-set B[,B2,...] [--plan]

  - Resume default: if cell_dir/report.json exists with terminal final_status -> skip.

  - Per-cell loop: write cell-state.json sentinel; invoke
    harness-adapters/<name> command < profile.json -> command-spec.json; compose
    task-spec; invoke task-executors/<name> < task-spec.json (writes
    cell_dir/result.json); compose report.json; delete cell-state.json.

description:
PROBLEM: ADR-013 §3 (decision item 4) requires pooled long-lived PTY sessions keyed by (harness, workdir) with `/clear` issued between turns, so consecutive Execute calls sharing a working directory reuse the same warm PTY session instead of paying Ink+auth cold-start each turn.

ROOT CAUSE:
- internal/harnesses/claude-tui/harness.go:32-33 — the Harness struct has no fields and holds no session pool, so there is nowhere to cache a warm session.
- internal/harnesses/claude-tui/harness.go:53-57 — Execute calls `go h.runTurn(...)` for every request with no pool lookup, spawning a fresh PTY per turn and defeating reuse.
- internal/harnesses/claude-tui/harness.go:60-79 — runTurn never writes `/clear` and never reuses a session; it only emits a stub Final event.
- internal/pty/session/types.go:176 — the Session type exposes no Pid() accessor (the pid lives only at internal/pty/session/session_unix.go:126 as `u.cmd.Process.Pid`), so session reuse cannot be asserted by pid identity.

PROPOSED FIX:
1. Add a package-scope session-pool singleton in internal/harnesses/claude-tui/ keyed by (harness, workdir) at depth 1 per key, placed at package scope rather than as a Harness/Runner field (ADR-013 §3 item 4 pool-placement rule), so two Harness instances share the pool. On Execute, look up an existing session for the workdir or open a new one via internal/pty/session.Start.
2. Between consecutive turns sharing a key, write `/clear` to the session and confirm the CLI acknowledged the clear (ready marker re-appears) before injecting the next prompt.
3. Add a Session.Pid() accessor in internal/pty/session exposing `u.cmd.Process.Pid` so reuse can be verified by pid identity.

- The PTY turn driver and intermediate ProgressEvent emission (sibling child A).

- Cassette-driven static fallback for production code (forbidden by fizeau-89eca738).
- Service-side changes beyond what child #1 already wired.
- Redesigning the hook-conflict arbitration layer.

Depends on child #1 and sibling child A. Governing artifacts: ADR-013 §3 (decision item 4), CONTRACT-004, internal/pty/ library.
